body:
## Summary
- Add missing S3 permissions discovered during CI/CD pipeline failures
- Add missing Budgets tagging permissions for Terraform state refresh
- Organize S3 section with comments for better readability

## Details

During the CI/CD pipeline fix (PRs #218, #219), we discovered several S3 and Budgets permissions that the IAM audit command didn't check for:

**S3 permissions added:**
- `s3:GetAccelerateConfiguration`, `s3:PutAccelerateConfiguration`
- `s3:GetBucketRequestPayment`
- `s3:GetBucketLogging`
- `s3:GetBucketNotification`
- `s3:GetReplicationConfiguration`
- `s3:GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration`
- `s3:GetBucketOwnershipControls`

**Budgets permissions added:**
- `budgets:DescribeBudgetActionsForBudget`
- `budgets:TagResource`
- `budgets:UntagResource`
- `budgets:ListTagsForResource`

The AWS Terraform provider reads ALL bucket attributes during `terraform plan`, requiring these Get* permissions even if the bucket doesn't use features like acceleration or logging.

## Test plan
- [ ] Run `/iam-audit` command and verify new permissions appear in checklist
- [ ] Confirm no syntax errors in the markdown file

author: agatti
body:
### Summary

This PR removes the `const` marker from the OpenAMP trace buffer, whose address is passed to libmetal's initialisation functions.

This was found whilst scanning the `.rodata` section of various ports, looking for ways to shrink MicroPython's footprint, as a continuation of the work for reducing pins' structures footprint.

I'm not sure this was intended, as there isn't much use in a read-only trace buffer (plus the comment for `fw_rsc_trace` in `lib/open-amp/lib/include/openamp/remoteproc.h` says the buffer is meant to be written to).

I've marked this PR as draft as it'd help to have some feedback from people who know how OpenAMP is used.  @iabdalkader, if you've got some time can you please check if this PR provides any benefits?

### Testing

I don't own any boards that use OpenAMP nor I'm familiar with that framework myself, so all I can look for is `openamp_trace_buf` appearing in the `.bss` section rather than in `.rodata` when looking at the mapfile for an OpenAMP-enabled image (eg. Alif Ensemble).

## Summary
- Add complete stack frame layout infrastructure for AArch64 backend
- Implement `StackSlot`, `StackFrame`, and `AArch64StackFrame` structures
- Support spill slot allocation, callee-saved register handling, and prologue/epilogue generation
- Integrate with register allocation system for spill slot management

This completes Phase 9 (Register Allocation) of the roadmap.

## Key Components

### Stack Slot Types
- `Spill(VReg)` - Spilled register storage
- `Local(Int)` - Local variable storage
- `OutgoingArg(Int)` - Outgoing call arguments
- `CalleeSaved(PReg)` - Saved callee-saved registers
- `ReturnAddress` - Return address (if needed)

### AArch64-specific Features
- 16-byte stack alignment
- Frame pointer (x29) and link register (x30) handling
- Automatic prologue/epilogue generation
- Integration with `build_stack_layout_aarch64` from regalloc results

## Test plan
- [x] All 287 tests pass (`moon test`)
- [x] Stack frame basic allocation test
- [x] Stack frame alignment test  
- [x] Callee-saved register handling test
- [x] Local variables allocation test
- [x] AArch64 frame setup test
- [x] AArch64 frame with spills test
- [x] Prologue/epilogue generation tests
- [x] Empty frame handling test

body:
# Pull Request Review and Merge Guidelines

## Pull Request Review Process

1. All pull requests must be reviewed by **at least two developers** before being merged into the `main` branch.
2. Reviewers should ensure:
   - The code follows the project's coding standards.
   - The functionality introduced by the pull request is working as expected.
   - There are no conflicts with the `main` branch.
3. Any required changes or improvements should be communicated via the pull request comments.
4. Once the pull request has been approved by two reviewers, it can be merged by one of the maintainers.

## Conflict Resolution

If there are conflicts with the `main` branch, the author of the pull request must resolve them before the pull request can be merged.

## Tests and Documentation

- Ensure all tests are passing before submitting a pull request.
- If the pull request introduces new functionality, make sure to update or add any necessary documentation.

body:
## Summary

This PR implements comprehensive test design guidelines and 9 template test files to systematize and improve test suite quality across the Chronia project. The guidelines provide structured approaches to equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis, and invalid input handling for temporal date functions.

## Changes

### 1. Documentation
- **docs/guidelines/test-design.md** (336 lines): 10-section comprehensive test design guideline
  - Section 1: Equivalence partitioning for numeric, date/time, and string parameters
  - Section 2: Boundary value analysis covering temporal edges, leap years, DST
  - Section 3-10: Invalid input handling, state-based testing, round-trip validation, locale testing, and edge case strategies

### 2. Template Test Files (9 files)
Standardized test templates for all function categories with real examples:
- `arithmetic.template.test.ts` - Addition/subtraction operations
- `boundary.template.test.ts` - Start/end of period operations
- `comparison.template.test.ts` - Date comparison functions
- `format-parse.template.test.ts` - Format and parse operations
- `getter.template.test.ts` - Value getter functions
- `setter.template.test.ts` - Value setter functions
- `truncation.template.test.ts` - Time truncation operations
- `utility.template.test.ts` - Utility functions
- `validation.template.test.ts` - Validation functions

### 3. Code Updates
- **package.json** (line 47): Updated `test:coverage` script to exclude PBT tests (`.kiro/specs/**/*.pbt.test.ts`) from coverage reports
- **tests/format.test.ts** (lines 461-552): Added 11 quote escaping test cases:
  - Literal text patterns (Class 2)
  - Escaped quote patterns (Class 3)
  - Mixed patterns (Class 4)
  - Coverage improved from 91.66% → 100%

## Key Features

### Test Design Guideline
- **Equivalence Partitioning**: Systematic classification of numeric, date/time, and string inputs
- **Boundary Value Analysis**: Temporal boundaries, leap years, month boundaries, DST transitions
- **Invalid Input Handling**: Clear patterns for Invalid Date, NaN, undefined, and type mismatches
- **State-Based Testing**: Testing operations that change internal state
- **Round-Trip Validation**: Format/parse consistency verification
- **Locale Testing**: Internationalization and locale-specific behavior
- **Edge Case Strategies**: Leap seconds, special date ranges, extreme values

### Template Structure
Each template includes:
- Function-specific testing notes
- Equivalence partitions with examples
- Boundary value test cases
- Invalid input test cases
- Type variation tests
- Real test implementations (not just stubs)

## Quality Verification

All quality checks passed:

- **TDD Tests**: 2576 tests passed (11 skipped)
- **PBT Tests**: 146 tests passed
- **Coverage**: 99.88% overall, 100% for format function
- **Code Lint**: 0 errors
- **Documentation Lint**: 0 errors (13 files)
- **TypeScript Build**: Success
- **Code Review**: EXCELLENT (no critical issues)

## Testing

### How to Test These Guidelines

1. **Review Test Design Guideline**:
   ```bash
   # Read the comprehensive guideline
   cat docs/guidelines/test-design.md
   ```

2. **Review Template Files**:
   ```bash
   # Examine a specific template
   cat docs/guidelines/test-templates/format-parse.template.test.ts
   ```

3. **Verify Coverage Improvement**:
   ```bash
   # Run coverage report (PBT tests now excluded)
   pnpm test:coverage
   ```

4. **Run All Tests**:
   ```bash
   pnpm test           # Run TDD tests (2576 tests)
   pnpm test:pbt       # Run property-based tests (146 tests)
   pnpm lint           # Run code linting (0 errors)
   pnpm lint:docs      # Run documentation linting (0 errors)
   ```

## Impact

### Immediate
- Establishes baseline test design standards for the project
- Provides reference templates for future test development
- Improves format function coverage to 100%
- Clarifies separation between unit test and property-based test metrics

### Future
- All new tests can follow the documented patterns
- Test coverage gaps can be systematically identified and addressed
- Test quality metrics can be consistently measured and improved
- New developers have clear guidance for writing tests

## Related Issues

Completes unit-test-review specification (`.kiro/specs/unit-test-review/`)
- Tasks completed: 5, 6, 7, 8
- All requirements met and validated

---

**Base**: `main`

body:
This PR enhances the `ai-check` command by implementing a live progress display using Server-Sent Events (SSE). It provides real-time feedback during test execution, including step updates, screenshot counts, and elapsed time.

## Changes
- **Live Progress**: Replaced polling with SSE streaming for real-time updates.
- **Compact & Verbose Modes**: Added a default compact view and a `--verbose` flag for detailed step-by-step output.
- **Log Persistence**: Execution logs are now saved to `.obs1/logs/` for debugging.
- **Cross-Platform Support**: Replaced `eventsource` with native `fetch` API for better compatibility and control.
- **UI Improvements**: Used `ora` and `chalk` for a polished CLI experience.

## Testing
- Verified `obs1 ai-check <id>` shows live progress in compact mode.
- Verified `obs1 ai-check --verbose <id>` shows detailed step outputs.
- Verified logs are correctly saved to `.obs1/logs/`.
- Verified screenshot counting and status updates.

body: # 🚩 연관 이슈 closed #376 # 📝 작업 내용 종소리를 조절할 수 있는 볼륨 바를 타이머 페이지에만 한정하여 헤더에 추가했어요. ## 세부 구현 내용 ### `CustomRangeSlider` 추가 종소리 조절을 포함하여 여러 목적으로 사용할 수 있는 슬라이더를 추가했어요. 아래 매개변수로 세부 사양을 조정할 수 있어요: ```ts interface CustomRangeSliderProps { value: number; // 슬라이더 값 onValueChange: (value: number) => void; // 슬라이더가 변경될 때 호출되는 함수 min?: number; // 최소값 max?: number; // 최대값 step?: number; // 간격 } ``` ### 종소리 훅에 볼륨 관련 개선 적용 종소리 훅 `useBellSound`에 볼륨 조절 관련 몇 가지 개선 사항을 적용하고 신규 기능을 추가했어요: - 원래는 아무것도 반환하지 않던 훅을, 볼륨 값과 볼륨 조절 함수를 호출하도록 변경 - 볼륨 값이 로컬 저장소 `localStorage`에 저장되도록 구현 ```ts export function useBellSound({ normalTimer, bells }: UseBellSoundProps) { const [volume, setVolume] = useState(() => { //... }); // ... // 디바운싱 관련 코드 useEffect(() => { const timerId = setTimeout(() => { localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, volume.toString()); }, 500); return () => clearTimeout(timerId); }, [volume]); // ... return { volume, setVolume }; } ``` 특히, 슬라이더는 마우스로 클릭한 후 이리저리 끌다 보면, 로컬 저장소로 새 값을 쓰는 작업이 여러 번 반복되어 성능 저하를 유발할 수 있어요. 이를 방지하기 위해 500 ms의 디바운싱을 적용하여, 사용자가 볼륨 조절을 완전히 끝낸 후에 볼륨 쓰기 작업이 실행되도록 구현했습니다. ### 타이머 페이지에 볼륨 바 추가 타이머 페이지에 볼륨 바를 추가했어요. 이 볼륨 바는 종소리가 울리는 타이머 페이지에만 필요하기 때문에, 다른 페이지에서는 보이지 않도록 TimerPage.tsx에 구현했어요. 기능의 세부 사항은 아래와 같아요: - 최소값 0, 최대값 10, 간격 1 - 볼륨이 0일 경우 음소거 상태로 간주 - 왼쪽 볼륨 버튼을 눌러 음소거 가능 - 볼륨 변경 시, 변경된 값을 `lastVolume` 변수에 저장하여 기억해 둠 - 음소거를 해제할 경우, 마지막 볼륨 값인 `lastVolume` 값을 복원 예를 들어, 사용자가 볼륨을 10에서 6으로 줄였다고 하면, 이 경우 `lastVolume`이 6으로 갱신돼요. 그리고 음소거를 할 경우 볼륨은 0이 되겠죠? 다시 음소거를 해제할 경우, `lastVolume`에 저장된 값이었던 6으로 복원되는 그런 시나리오입니다. # 🏞️ 스크린샷 (선택) ## 마우스 호버 시 표시되는 실제 볼륨 값 ## 음소거 여부에 따른 음소거 버튼 ### 음소거 X ### 음소거 O # 🗣️ 리뷰 요구사항 (선택) - 써니가 디자인 관련 개선을 요청할 경우, UI 관련 코드는 수정될 수도 있습니다. - 잘 동작하는지 확인해주시면 감사하겠습니다! ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **새로운 기능** * 타이머 페이지에 볼륨 버튼과 토글형 볼륨바 추가 * 음소거 토글 및 마지막 볼륨 복원 기능을 가진 VolumeBar 추가 * 0–10 스케일의 커스텀 슬라이더(툴팁 포함) 및 새로운 볼륨 아이콘 추가 * 벨소리 재생용 볼륨 제어(볼륨 조회·업데이트 API) 및 로컬 저장·디바운스 반영 * **기타 변경** * 스티키 헤더·모달의 쌓임 순서(z-index) 조정 * 관련 컴포넌트용 Storybook 스토리 추가 ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings.

author: kkm-horikawa
body:
# Release v0.2.0: Slot-Based Templating System This PR merges the complete v0.2.0 slot-based templating system implementation from `develop` to `main`. ## 🎉 New Features ### Slot-Based Templating System - **ReusableLayoutBlock** - New block type for layout templates with fillable slots - **SlotFillBlock** - Block for injecting custom content into layout slots - **Slot Detection API** - Endpoint for detecting slots in layout templates (`/admin/reusable-blocks/blocks/{id}/slots/`) - **Dynamic Slot Selection UI** - JavaScript widget with auto-populated dropdowns - **Nested Layout Support** - Layouts can be nested within slots (with known limitation tracked in #62) - **Default Content Preservation** - Unfilled slots display their default content ### Developer Experience - BeautifulSoup4 for robust HTML parsing - Slot rendering utilities (`render_layout_with_slots`) - Extended circular reference detection for slot-based nesting - Improved error messages with reference chains (e.g., "Layout A → Layout B → Layout A") ### Configuration - `SLOT_ATTRIBUTE` - Customizable HTML attribute for slots (default: `data-slot`) - `SLOT_LABEL_ATTRIBUTE` - Optional label attribute (default: `data-slot-label`) - `RENDER_TIMEOUT` - Maximum render time limit (default: 5 seconds) ## 📚 Documentation ### README.md - Added "Choosing the Right Block" guide comparing v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 - Complete slot-based templating tutorial with step-by-step examples - Enhanced troubleshooting section with slot-specific solutions - Updated configuration reference with v0.2.0 settings ### CHANGELOG.md (NEW) - Comprehensive changelog following Keep a Changelog format - Complete v0.2.0 release notes - Migration guide (no breaking changes!) ### ARCHITECTURE.md - Design decision rationale for HTML attribute-based slots - Detailed slot rendering pipeline documentation - Performance characteristics and optimization notes ## 🧪 Testing ### End-to-End Tests - 8 comprehensive E2E tests (7 passing, 1 skipped) - Complete workflow verification from layout creation to rendering - v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 compatibility testing ### CI Status - ✅ Type Check - ✅ Lint - ✅ All 39 Python/Django/Wagtail combinations ## 🔄 Backward Compatibility **v0.2.0 is fully backward compatible with v0.1.0:** - Existing `ReusableBlockChooserBlock` continues to work as before - No database migrations required - Existing ReusableBlocks work without changes - v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 blocks can be used together in the same page ## 📝 Migration Guide To start using slot-based templating: 1. **Add URLs** (required for slot detection): ```python # urls.py urlpatterns = [ path('admin/reusable-blocks/', include('wagtail_reusable_blocks.urls')), ] ``` 2. **Create a layout** with `data-slot` attributes: ```html

Default content

``` 3. **Use ReusableLayoutBlock** in your page models: ```python from wagtail_reusable_blocks.blocks import ReusableLayoutBlock body = StreamField([ ('layout', ReusableLayoutBlock()), ]) ``` ## 🐛 Known Issues - **Nested Layout Rendering** (#62) - BeautifulSoup append error when rendering nested layouts. Workaround: Don't nest ReusableLayoutBlock within slots. Fix planned for v0.2.1. ## 📦 Related Issues Closes #2, #47, #48, #49, #50, #51, #52, #53

   - 每个核心概念（软标签、温度、KL散度）都有层层递进的剖析
   - 从现象到本质，从"是什么"到"为什么"

2. **信息论视角**
   - 用信息论解释温度对分布熵的影响
   - 深入分析 KL 散度的非对称性及其蒸馏意义
   - $T^2$ 补偿因子的数学推导

3. **实践导向的技术洞察**
   - 具体的调参策略（温度选择、α 调优、学习率设置）
   - 显存优化的权衡考量
   - 教师模型状态管理的技术细节

4. **逻辑递进与语言承接**
   - 每节开头回顾上文，结尾引出下一个问题
   - 使用"为什么"、"那么"等过渡词自然衔接

5. **独到见解**
   - 软标签的"信息富集"概念
   - Softmax 的"自信陷阱"
   - 知识的"压缩性"与蒸馏的本质联系
   - KL 散度前向/反向方向的深层含义

- [x] Understand the issue: Charging power sometimes stays at 0W during charging
- [x] Explore the codebase and understand how charging power is handled
- [x] Identify the root cause: When API returns incomplete data (no voltage/current), charging_power becomes 0/None
- [x] Implement fix: Retain last valid charging power value when currently charging but API returns 0/None
- [x] Add test to verify the fix
- [x] Run linting and tests
- [x] Run code review

## Changes

The fix ensures that when charging is active (CHARGING or DC_CHARGING status) and the API temporarily returns 0 for charging power, the sensor retains the last valid non-zero value instead of jumping to 0W.

Key changes:
1. Reordered the logic in `SmartHashtagBatteryRangeSensor.native_value` to check charging status BEFORE the early return for `-0.0`, allowing the retention logic to work correctly
2. Store valid non-zero charging power values for future use
3. Return the stored value when charging is active but API returns 0/None
4. Fixed undefined `_last_value` references to use `_last_valid_value`
5. Added comprehensive test `test_charging_power_retains_value_during_charging` to verify the fix

## Follow-up: Linter Configuration Discrepancy

**Issue discovered**: The pre-commit config runs both `ruff` and `flake8`, but they have different rule coverage. F824 (unused `nonlocal`) is caught by flake8 but not by ruff with current settings. Developers running only `ruff check` locally will miss some errors that CI catches.

**Suggested fix**: Either:
- Update developer documentation to recommend running `pre-commit run --all-files` locally
- Or update `ruff.toml` to include equivalent checks to flake8
- Or consolidate to a single linter to avoid discrepancies

body:
## 概要
支出ビューで発生していた3つの問題を修正しました：
1. 府省庁(TopN以外)ノードが表示されない
2. 事業(TopN以外)ノードが重複して表示される
3. 支出先バッジのカウントが不正確

## 問題の詳細

### 再現手順
1. 支出先「総務省」を選択して支出ビューへ遷移
2. 設定パネルで以下に変更：
   - 支出元事業TopN = 10
   - 支出元府省庁TopN = 1
3. サンキー図を確認

### 問題の症状
- ✗ `府省庁(Top1以外)`ノードが表示されない
- ✗ `事業(Top10以外)`ノードが2つ表示される
- ✗ 支出先バッジが「2」と表示される（実際は1つ）

## 原因分析

### 問題1: 府省庁(TopN以外)ノードが表示されない
`app/lib/sankey-generator.ts` のline 794-868で、以下の2つの金額が合算されていました：
- TopN府省庁からの「事業(TopN以外)」への支出
- TopN以外の府省庁からの支出

これらが1つの「事業(TopN以外)」ノードに合算されたため、府省庁レベルの分離ができていませんでした。

### 問題2: 事業ノードの重複
同じ名前`事業(TopN以外)`のノードがColumn 1とColumn 2に作成されていましたが、これは本来別のノード（TopN府省庁からの事業 vs TopN以外府省庁からの事業）であるべきでした。

### 問題3: 支出先バッジのカウント問題
`metadata.summary.selectedSpendings` の計算で、支出ビューでも `selection.topSpendings.length` を使用していましたが、支出ビューでは常に1つの受給者を表示するため、カウントは常に1であるべきでした。

## 修正内容

### バックエンド変更（app/lib/sankey-generator.ts）

#### 1. ノード構造の分離（line 794-936）

**TopN府省庁からの「事業(TopN以外)」ノード** (line 794-862)
```typescript
// Column 1
{
  id: 'project-budget-other-spending-view',
  name: `事業(Top${projectLimit}以外)`,
  type: 'project-budget',
}

// Column 2
{
  id: 'project-spending-other-spending-view',
  name: `事業(Top${projectLimit}以外)`,
  type: 'project-spending',
}

// リンク: TopN府省庁 → 事業予算(TopN以外) → 事業支出(TopN以外) → 受給者
```

**TopN以外の府省庁ノード** (line 864-936) - 新規追加
```typescript
// Column 0
{
  id: 'ministry-budget-other-spending-view',
  name: `府省庁(Top${ministryLimit}以外)`,
  type: 'ministry-budget',
}

// Column 1
{
  id: 'project-budget-other-ministry-spending-view',
  name: `事業(Top${ministryLimit}以外府省庁)`,
  type: 'project-budget',
}

// Column 2
{
  id: 'project-spending-other-ministry-spending-view',
  name: `事業(Top${ministryLimit}以外府省庁)`,
  type: 'project-spending',
}

// リンク: 府省庁(TopN以外) → 事業予算 → 事業支出 → 受給者
```

#### 2. メタデータ修正（line 138）
```typescript
selectedSpendings: targetRecipientName ? 1 : selection.topSpendings.length
```

### フロントエンド変更（app/sankey/page.tsx）

新しいノード名パターンに対応する正規表現を更新（4箇所）：

**1. ノードクリックハンドラー** (line 254)
```typescript
// Before
if (actualNode.name.match(/^事業\(Top\d+以外\)$/))

// After
if (actualNode.name.match(/^事業\(Top\d+以外.*\)$/))
```

**2. カラーマッピング** (line 669)
```typescript
if (name.match(/^事業\(Top\d+以外.*\)$/))
```

**3. クリック可否判定** (line 750)
```typescript
!nodeName.match(/^事業\(Top\d+以外.*\)$/)
```

**4. ツールチップ表示** (line 814)
```typescript
if (name.match(/^事業\(Top\d+以外.*\)$/))
```

## テスト方法

### 手動テスト
1. http://localhost:3000/sankey にアクセス
2. 支出先「総務省」を選択
3. 設定パネルで以下に変更：
   - 支出元事業TopN = 10
   - 支出元府省庁TopN = 1
4. 以下を確認：
   - ✅ `府省庁(Top1以外)`ノードがColumn 0に表示される
   - ✅ `事業(Top1以外府省庁)`ノードがColumn 1とColumn 2に表示される
   - ✅ `事業(Top10以外)`ノードが別途Column 1とColumn 2に表示される
   - ✅ 支出先バッジが「1」と表示される
   - ✅ ノードクリックが正常に動作する
   - ✅ カラーリング（グレー）が正しく適用される

### 確認ポイント
- ✅ 府省庁(TopN以外)ノードが正しく表示される
- ✅ ノードの重複がない
- ✅ 支出先バッジのカウントが正確
- ✅ ノード名のパターンマッチングが動作する
- ✅ 既存のビュー（全体、府省庁、事業）に影響なし

## 影響範囲
- ✅ 支出ビューのノード生成ロジック
- ✅ 支出ビューのメタデータ計算
- ✅ フロントエンドのノード名パターンマッチング
- ✅ 全体ビュー、府省庁ビュー、事業ビューには影響なし

## データフロー

### 修正前
```
TopN府省庁 ─┐
            ├→ 事業(TopN以外) → 支出先
TopN以外府省庁┘  (重複・混在)
```

### 修正後
```
TopN府省庁 → 事業(Top10以外) → 支出先
府省庁(Top1以外) → 事業(Top1以外府省庁) → 支出先
```

Fixes #11

This pull request introduces several updates to the release and build workflows, dependency versions, and adds version reporting to the CLI tools. The main improvements include updating CI workflows to use the latest actions and Go versions, modernizing dependency management, and adding a `--version` flag to the CLI for easier version tracking.

**CI/CD and Release Workflow Updates:**

* Updated `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `.github/workflows/test.yml` to use newer versions of GitHub Actions, Go (now testing/building against 1.24 and 1.25), and GoReleaser (v6), and switched release triggers to the `main` branch for more standard release management. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-87db21a973eed4fef5f32b267aa60fcee5cbdf03c67fafdc2a9b553bb0b15f34L6-R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-faff1af3d8ff408964a57b2e475f69a6b7c7b71c9978cccc8f471798caac2c88L8-R29)
* Added a `.tagpr` configuration file to automate release candidate PRs and tagging, specifying release branch, version file, and release behavior.

**Dependency and Configuration Modernization:**

* Updated the Go version in `go.mod` to 1.23 and bumped AWS SDK dependencies to the latest versions, with improved indirect dependency tracking.
* Added a `version: 2` field to `.goreleaser.yml` and updated snapshot naming to use `version_template` for compatibility with newer GoReleaser releases. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-42e26dc67aed8aa3edb2472b4403288c1699fb6dc47419b9a475f0f224fe4689R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-42e26dc67aed8aa3edb2472b4403288c1699fb6dc47419b9a475f0f224fe4689L34-R35)

body:
## Summary Fixes #6 When "Individual Translations" is enabled, hovering multi-word meaning blocks caused the translation to disappear when moving the mouse over whitespace between words. ### Root Cause The original implementation attached hover listeners to individual `` elements. Whitespace between words isn't part of any span, so moving the mouse to whitespace triggered `mouseleave` with no corresponding `mouseenter`. ### Solution Wrap each meaning block's spans in an inline `` container element. Using `Range.extractContents()`, the wrapper captures both the spans AND the whitespace text nodes between them. **Before:** ```html

the quick brown

``` **After:** ```html

the quick brown

``` A single hover listener on the wrapper covers the **entire visual area** of the meaning block, including whitespace. ### Key Changes - **`wrapMeaningBlockSpans()`**: Wraps spans in inline container using Range - **`unwrapMeaningBlock()`**: Restores original DOM on cleanup - **`renderSegmentations()`**: Creates wrappers, attaches hover to wrapper - **`clearOverlays()`**: Properly unwraps spans when clearing - Removed `setupHoverListeners()` (no longer needed) - Added `.elt-meaning-block` CSS class ## Test plan - [ ] Load extension in Chrome (`chrome://extensions` -> Load unpacked or reload) - [ ] Navigate to an elevenreader.io article with translations processed - [ ] Ensure "Individual Translations" toggle is ON in popup - [ ] Hover over a multi-word meaning block - [ ] Move the mouse between words (over whitespace) - [ ] **Verify translation stays visible** while anywhere in the block - [ ] Move mouse outside the block - [ ] **Verify translation hides** immediately - [ ] Click on words to seek audio - **verify clicks still work** - [ ] Hold the "文" button - verify all translations still appear

author: weiiiiying
body:
## **Addressed Issue**

The `MathUtils` utility class had several issues:

* No private constructor, allowing unintended instantiation.
* `gcd()` failed on zero values and didn’t correctly handle negatives.
* `lcm()` could overflow when multiplying large integers.
* Array-based methods lacked input validation (null/empty arrays or null elements).
* JavaDoc was incomplete, missing explanations of formulas, edge cases, and exceptions.

## **Reengineering Details**

The following improvements were implemented:

* **Added private constructor** to enforce the utility class pattern.
* **Reworked `gcd()` implementation** to correctly handle zero and negative inputs, and extracted recursive logic into a private helper.
* **Improved `lcm()`** by using `(m / gcd) * n` to avoid overflow and adding zero checks.
* **Added defensive validation** to array-based GCD/LCM methods (null array, empty array, null elements).
* **Expanded JavaDoc** with mathematical definitions, parameter constraints, edge cases, and exception documentation.

## **Reengineering Strategy**

* Used **defensive programming** to validate inputs early and avoid runtime errors.
* Applied **edge-case analysis** to ensure correct mathematical behavior for zero, negative numbers, and large values.
* **Refactored code** for readability and maintainability (helper method, clearer structure).
* Followed **existing utility class patterns** in the codebase for consistency.
* Enhanced documentation so behavior is fully defined and predictable.

## **Impact of the Changes**

* **Increased robustness**: prevents division-by-zero, null pointer issues, and integer overflow.
* **Better developer experience** through clear errors and complete documentation.
* **Improved maintainability** with cleaner structure and self-explanatory JavaDoc.
* **No breaking changes**: behavior for all valid inputs remains the same.

Slack error messages in `slack-error-handler.ts` were hardcoded in Japanese without i18n support.

body:
Addresses code review feedback from PR #71: missing `errdefer` statements for etag allocations could lead to memory leaks if errors occur after allocation but before return.

## Changes

Added defensive `errdefer self.allocator.free(etag);` after etag allocations in 4 locations:

- `.force` mode (line 264)
- `.never` mode "too large file" case (line 283)
- `.auto` mode "too large file" case (line 361)
- `getCachedContentWithETag` function (line 386)

```zig
const etag = try generateETag(self.allocator, stat.size, stat.mtime);
errdefer self.allocator.free(etag);  // Added
return .{ .content = content, .etag = etag };
```

Ensures consistent memory management patterns across all code paths and guards against future changes that might introduce error-producing operations before return.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Fixes a performance issue where the audio unmute logic was being called excessively, causing console spam and potential frame stuttering. The previous implementation registered `mousemove` and `mouseenter` event listeners that would call `tryUnmuteAudio()` on every mouse movement. When the browser blocked autoplay (which is common), this resulted in 50+ error logs per second during gameplay.

**Changes:**
- Added `audioUnmuteAttempted` flag to prevent repeated unmute attempts while one is in progress
- Removed high-frequency event listeners (`mousemove`, `mouseenter`) - audio now only unmutes on `click`, `keydown`, or `touchstart`
- Removed noisy console.log on failure (the error was being logged dozens of times per second)
- Updated version display to PR#36

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify console is clean during gameplay**: Open DevTools console, play the game, and confirm there are no repeated "Audio unmute blocked" messages
- [ ] **Verify audio still works**: After clicking any button or pressing a key, background music should start playing
- [ ] **Test if stuttering is reduced**: Move back and forth rapidly in multiplayer mode - check if the stuttering/lag is improved compared to before

**Test plan:**
1. Open the preview URL (should show "PR#36" in bottom-right)
2. Open browser DevTools console before interacting with the page
3. Move mouse around - should NOT see repeated audio error messages
4. Click a button - audio should start playing
5. Start a multiplayer match and test movement smoothness

### Notes

This fix addresses the audio spam that was identified as a potential cause of the movement stuttering reported by the user. If stuttering persists after this fix, there may be other contributing factors (server position corrections, camera smoothing, etc.) that need investigation.

Issue reported that clicking time slots didn't open the appointment modal, and "Start survey" never fired—suspected missing modal HTML and a bug nulling out the appointment ID before survey start. **Verification Results** After investigation, the codebase already contains the correct implementation: - **Modal HTML** (`pwa/index.html:109-159`): Complete modal structure with all form fields (customer name, lead ID, address, postcode, phone, notes, system type) and Save/Start survey buttons - **`saveAppointmentFromModal`** (`pwa/app.js:308-360`): Correctly preserves `targetId`, updates `AppState.currentAppointmentId` before calling `startSurveyForAppointment()` - **`closeAppointmentModal`** (`pwa/app.js:303-306`): Does not clear `currentAppointmentId` No code changes required—functionality matches the specification from the issue.
Original prompt Nice catch – that actually tells us exactly where things are broken. Short version: 👉 If appointments don’t open, it almost always means the appointment modal HTML isn’t in the page, so when the JS tries to open it, it hits null and silently dies. That would also explain why “Start survey” never fires, because that button lives inside the modal that never appears. Let’s fix this in two tiny steps. ⸻ 1️⃣ Add the appointment modal HTML (index.html) In pwa/index.html, just before , make sure you have this whole block. If it’s missing, add it. Appointment

author: lihaoyi
body:
Rather than just being a dumb wrapper of `error: String`, it now basically is a `List[(error: String, path: os.Path = null, index: Int = -1)]`. Failures can then be combined with `Failure.combine`, and this lets us defer rendering until "later" so that the code reporting a failure doesn't need to be aware of the intricacies of formatting and rendering errors.

For backwards-compatibility purposes this is implemented as an intrusive linked list, with the `path` and `index` fields optional and an optional `next: Option[Failure]` field pointing to the next one. Someone who uses `Failure` naively as before would simply get the first `error` while being unaware of the other fields, which is probably fine.

author: copilot
body:
Device should be inferred from evaluation context (Start node), not wired explicitly to terminal nodes. Do Nothing node's first slot becomes a trigger accepting any signal type.

## Changes

- **ExecuteActionNode**: Removed `device` input. Device now read from `ExecutionInputs.device` at runtime.
- **DoNothingNode**: Replaced `device` input with `trigger` input of type `Any`. Any upstream signal terminates evaluation.
- **Execution engine**: Updated `evaluate_execute_action_node` and `evaluate_do_nothing_node` to use context device.

## Example

Before:
```
Start ──[device]──> Execute Action
       ──[device]──> Do Nothing
```

After:
```
Start ──────────────> Execute Action (device inferred)
       ──[any signal]──> Do Nothing (device inferred)
```

Start node retains device output for device-specific logic branching.

author: rbrinkke
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: snakeland
body:
## Problem
The CI workflow shows a warning: `Context access might be invalid: CODECOV_TOKEN` because the Codecov token might not be accessible in certain contexts (like PRs from forks).

## Solution
Added `fail_ci_if_error: false` to the Codecov upload step.

## What This Does
- ✅ **Prevents CI failures** when Codecov token is unavailable
- ✅ **Silences warnings** about invalid context access
- ✅ **Workflow continues successfully** even if coverage upload fails
- ✅ **Useful for fork PRs** where repository secrets aren't available

## Behavior
- **On push to main**: Coverage uploads successfully ✅
- **On PRs from main repo**: Coverage uploads successfully ✅  
- **On PRs from forks**: Coverage upload fails gracefully, CI passes ✅
- **Coverage still collected**: Test coverage runs and displays in all cases

## Testing
CI will pass even if Codecov upload encounters issues, while still collecting and reporting coverage in the test output.

body:
The codebase had leftover Puppeteer dependencies and hardcoded credentials despite migrating to a remote VPS scraper architecture. Health endpoints needed to proxy directly to the remote service.

## Changes

### Removed Puppeteer
- Dropped `puppeteer` from `package.json`
- Cleaned `livesoccertv.js` – marked DEPRECATED, removed all browser automation code
- Zero puppeteer references remain in the codebase

### Fixed Health Endpoints
- `/health/lstv` now proxies directly via axios to `${LSTV_SCRAPER_URL}/health`
- `/health/tsdb` returns proper error structure on failure
- Added axios import to `app.js`

### Security: Required Environment Variables
- Removed hardcoded default credentials from health endpoint and `scrapers/lstv.js`
- `LSTV_SCRAPER_URL` and `LSTV_SCRAPER_KEY` are now required – clear error returned if missing
- Removed deprecated `liveSoccerTvUsePuppeteer` config option

```javascript
// Health endpoint now validates required env vars
app.get('/health/lstv', async (req, res) => {
  const LSTV_SCRAPER_URL = process.env.LSTV_SCRAPER_URL;
  const LSTV_SCRAPER_KEY = process.env.LSTV_SCRAPER_KEY;
  
  if (!LSTV_SCRAPER_URL || !LSTV_SCRAPER_KEY) {
    return res.status(500).json({
      ok: false,
      error: 'LSTV_SCRAPER_URL and LSTV_SCRAPER_KEY environment variables must be configured'
    });
  }
  // ... proxy to remote service
});
```

### Documentation
- Updated README: required env vars table, scraper architecture section
- Added comments to all scraper modules noting they're HTTP-based (no Puppeteer)

body:
Port of the ZON (Zero Overhead Notation) format from [zon-ts](https://github.com/ZON-Format/zon-ts) to Java. ZON achieves 23.8% token reduction vs JSON while maintaining 100% LLM retrieval accuracy.

## Core Implementation
- `Zon` - Static `encode()`/`decode()` API
- `ZonEncoder` - Table encoding for uniform arrays, `T`/`F` booleans, canonical number formatting
- `ZonDecoder` - Strict/non-strict modes, dotted key expansion, CSV+JSON escape handling
- `ZonDecodeError` - Error codes E001-E304 with line/context info
- `Cli` - Command-line `encode`/`decode` for JSON↔ZON conversion

## Test Suite (92 tests)
- Round-trip codec tests
- Conformance tests (encoder/decoder spec compliance)
- Strict mode validation (row/field count mismatches)
- Security tests (prototype pollution, DOS limits, circular refs)

## Documentation
- README, SPEC.md, API reference, syntax cheatsheet, LLM best practices
- Benchmark reports copied from zon-ts

## Usage

```java
// Encode
Map<String, Object> data = Map.of("name", "Alice", "active", true);
String zon = Zon.encode(data);
// active:T
// name:Alice

// Decode (strict mode default)
Object decoded = Zon.decode(zon);

// Decode (non-strict)
Object decoded = Zon.decode(zon, false);
```

body:
This pull request introduces a new framework for pairwise evaluation of experiment runs, allowing direct comparison of outputs from two experiments using LLM-based judges. The main changes include adding pairwise evaluators and prompt templates, updating the CLI to support pairwise mode, and integrating these evaluators into the module API.

**Pairwise Evaluation Framework**

* Added a new module `pairwise_evaluators.py` implementing four pairwise evaluators (helpfulness, hallucination, coherence, completeness) that compare responses from two experiments using LLM prompts and scoring logic. Includes factory and lookup functions for flexible usage.
* Created `pairwise_prompts.py` containing prompt templates for each pairwise criterion, designed to elicit comparative judgments from the LLM.

**Command-line Interface Enhancements**

* Updated `scripts/run_evals.py` to add `--pairwise` and `--experiments` CLI options, enabling users to run pairwise evaluations between two experiments. Includes argument validation and invokes the new evaluators and prompt logic.
* Imported the new pairwise evaluators in `run_evals.py` and exposed them in the module API for easier access. body:
This pull request primarily updates the `nav2_params.yaml` configuration for the navigation stack by cleaning up redundant node-specific parameter blocks, refining costmap plugin selections, and tuning parameters for smoother operation. The changes aim to simplify configuration, ensure consistency in simulation time usage, and introduce the velocity smoother component.

**Configuration cleanup and simplification:**

* Removed redundant `*_rclcpp_node` parameter blocks (such as `amcl_map_client`, `amcl_rclcpp_node`, `bt_navigator_rclcpp_node`, `controller_server_rclcpp_node`, and `planner_server_rclcpp_node`) to reduce duplication and potential confusion about where `use_sim_time` and other parameters are set. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-caee0063be400f605d9d89ba26571a12e5a05806fe37eb8779da763ef1e924c2L71-L78) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-caee0063be400f605d9d89ba26571a12e5a05806fe37eb8779da763ef1e924c2L124-L127) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-caee0063be400f605d9d89ba26571a12e5a05806fe37eb8779da763ef1e924c2L245-L248) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-caee0063be400f605d9d89ba26571a12e5a05806fe37eb8779da763ef1e924c2L498-L522)
* Removed the `recoveries_server` parameter block, likely consolidating recovery configuration elsewhere or relying on defaults.

**Costmap and plugin configuration:**

* Updated the `plugins` lists for both `local_costmap` and `global_costmap` to remove commented-out alternatives and clarify the active plugin set, focusing on layers like `top_obstacle_layer`, `obstacle_layer`, `denoise_layer`, and `inflation_layer`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-caee0063be400f605d9d89ba26571a12e5a05806fe37eb8779da763ef1e924c2L265-L270) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-caee0063be400f605d9d89ba26571a12e5a05806fe37eb8779da763ef1e924c2L367-L370)

**Parameter tuning:**

* Adjusted the `expected_planner_frequency` for `planner_server` from 10.0 (commented out) to 1.0, indicating a lower planning frequency.
* Modified the `costmap_filter_info_server` parameters, increasing `multiplier` from `-0.8` to `-0.6` for filter tuning.

**New feature addition:**

* Added configuration for the `velocity_smoother` node, including documentation reference and commented-out velocity limits, to enable smoother velocity commands.

Comprehensive technical analysis of the DealersChoice monolithic web app to support migration to a new API-based backend. Documents the full stack: ASP.NET Core 7.0 + React 18 SPA + MongoDB/SQL Server + SignalR + VideoSDK.

## Report Contents (`ARCHITECTURE_REPORT.md`)

- **Architecture Overview**: Solution structure, startup config, service registrations
- **Controllers**: 6 API controllers (no MVC views), 35+ game actions in `GameController`
- **SignalR Hubs**: `GameClass` hub with full event catalog for real-time game state sync
- **Client-Side**: React/Redux structure, state slices, API communication patterns
- **Video Integration**: VideoSDK.live flow with credit tracking
- **Domain Models**: `GameHash`, `ActivePlayer`, `Card` MongoDB schemas
- **Database Access**: MongoDB primary (game state), SQL Server legacy (unused)
- **Migration Notes**: Coupling hotspots, duplicated client/server logic, critical file checklist

## Key Findings

| Area | Issue |
|------|-------|
| `GameController.cs` | 35+ actions with embedded business logic, no domain layer |
| State duplication | Turn/bet logic duplicated in C# and `gameStateSlice.js` |
| SignalR coupling | Controllers directly broadcast to hub clients |

## Migration Priority Files

```
Controllers/GameController.cs       # Extract game engine
Controllers/AuthController.cs       # Replace with API auth
Hubs/GameClass.cs                   # Design new hub contract

- **IConsentRepository**: Repository interface for consent data access operations
- **IConsentService**: Service interface for consent operations

- **ConsentService**: Business logic for consent operations
- **ConsentSeeder**: Seeds default consent types at application startup
- **BuyerDbContext**: Updated with consent entity configurations

### Database
- Migration for ConsentTypes, ConsentVersions, and UserConsents tables with proper indexes

### Web Layer
- Updated registration page to display and collect consent preferences during signup
- New Privacy Settings page for buyers to view and manage their consent preferences

body:
Overlay-side PR: https://github.com/tosuapp/counters/pull/64

This PR introduces API versioning for overlays using v2 and Precise APIs by processing the `v` query parameter. If the overlay doesn't specify the version it wants to use (or the value is invalid), tosu will send the first version of an API, ensuring backwards compatibility. You can also get JSON response previews by adding the `v` parameter to the URL, if omitted or invalid - tosu will send the latest version of an API

---

I also wanted to document this in the wiki, but I guess it's not possible to PR wikis, so if you want to add it, then here:
<details>
<summary>The wiki article</summary>

````
Starting with tosu X.Y.Z, you can use different versions of v2 and Precise APIs to get more accurate data

## How to use

You can use new versions of APIs in two ways:
1. Using tosu's `socket.js`
2. Using `WebSocket`/`ReconnectingWebSocket` directly

> [!NOTE]
> The API version must be a positive integer. If the value is omitted or invalid (e.g. `-5`, `null`, `"undefined"`, `"abc123"`), the **version 1** of an API will be used. If the version is a fractional number, the decimal component gets truncated (e.g. `3.14159 -> 3` - version 3 will be used)

### Using tosu's `socket.js`

Ensure your `socket.js` is at least version **0.2.0** - if it's an older version, [download the new version](https://github.com/tosuapp/counters/blob/master/quickstart/js/socket.js)

When connecting with either of the APIs, the function signature now looks like this:
```js
socket.api_v2(callback, filters, apiVersion)
socket.api_v2_precise(callback, filters, apiVersion)
```

Callback and [filters](https://github.com/tosuapp/tosu/wiki/Apply-filters-to-websocket) remain the same, `apiVersion` is an optional parameter

### Using `WebSocket`/`ReconnectingWebSocket` directly

Simply add the `v` parameter to the WebSocket URL:
```js
const socket = new ReconnectingWebSocket(`ws://${window.location.host}/websocket/v2?v=6`);
```

## JSON Response Previews

You can get a preview of how the data is structured in different version by simply adding the `v` URL parameter to the URL:
- `/json/v2?v=2`
- `/json/v2/precise?v=2`

> [!NOTE]
> The API version must be a positive integer. If the value is omitted or invalid (e.g. `-5`, `null`, `"undefined"`, `"abc123"`), the **latest version** of an API will be used. If the version is a fractional number, the decimal component gets truncated (e.g. `3.14159 -> 3` - version 3 will be used)

## Version History

### Version 1

Initial version


### Version 2

#### Precise API

`keys` is now an array of keys in both tourney and regular data:
```ts
interface KeyOverlayButton {
    name: string;
    isPressed: boolean;
    count: number;
}
```

Examples:
- osu!catch in osu!(stable)
```json
{
    "currentTime": 0,
    "keys": [
        {
            "name": "L",
            "isPressed": false,
            "count": 0
        },
        {
            "name": "R",

        },

This pull request introduces password-based authentication to the OpenMemory dashboard, ensuring that only authorized users can access the web interface. It adds secure login and logout functionality, environment variable configuration for the dashboard password, and middleware to enforce authentication across dashboard routes.

**Authentication and Security**

* Added password authentication for dashboard access, including a login API route (`dashboard/app/api/auth/login/route.ts`) that validates credentials and sets a secure, HTTP-only cookie for session management. (`[dashboard/app/api/auth/login/route.tsR1-R43](diffhunk://#diff-ad0d2869a74d8b183558597ca13dbb381cc12947e6335e778414f05872631707R1-R43)`)
* Implemented logout functionality with an API route (`dashboard/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts`) that clears the authentication cookie. (`[dashboard/app/api/auth/logout/route.tsR1-R16](diffhunk://#diff-40bdfb02cbcd9c8fb24c902fbbe3b02f9e9ad6a77bf1da3891f2e6ab819cb5adR1-R16)`)
* Introduced middleware (`dashboard/middleware.ts`) to protect dashboard routes, redirecting unauthenticated users to the login page and preventing access to the login page when already authenticated. (`[dashboard/middleware.tsR1-R33](diffhunk://#diff-9ff02c8a401e035549081404c7861017fa3e36ade9fb93d897e6fd0c39d75eb7R1-R33)`)

**User Interface Updates**

* Added a login page (`dashboard/app/login/page.tsx`) for users to enter the dashboard password, with error handling and session expiration messaging. (`[dashboard/app/login/page.tsxR1-R87](diffhunk://#diff-6c5bd06ddb9c67f0ddd75e2adf5aa2a51d073d84a9781af2665107d898b76e8fR1-R87)`)
* Updated the dashboard navbar (`dashboard/components/navbar.tsx`) to include a logout button that triggers the logout API and redirects to the login page. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c1d39079765cf60e109bc7611084b88b675764641baa241a936edc03d5abbe5bR4-R10)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c1d39079765cf60e109bc7611084b88b675764641baa241a936edc03d5abbe5bR39-R50)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c1d39079765cf60e109bc7611084b88b675764641baa241a936edc03d5abbe5bL55)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c1d39079765cf60e109bc7611084b88b675764641baa241a936edc03d5abbe5bL69-R90)`)

**Configuration**

* Added `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` environment variable to example files (`.env.example`, `dashboard/.env.local.example`), and updated deployment configs (`docker-compose.yml`, `render.yaml`) to support secure password configuration. - Registering package: Sunny
- Repository: https://github.com/SunnySuite/Sunny.jl
- Created by: @kbarros
- Version: v0.8.0
- Commit: 47a4453f5a76ea451d3b0854ee57be3d58faa315
- Reviewed by: @kbarros
- Reference: https://github.com/SunnySuite/Sunny.jl/commit/47a4453f5a76ea451d3b0854ee57be3d58faa315#commitcomment-171658383
- Description: Spin dynamics and generalization to SU(N) coherent states
- Release notes:
<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
`````
**Breaking changes** in this release.

* Significant enhancements to crystal construction and symmetry analysis, which may **reorder certain atom and site indices** (#421). Crystal lattice vectors and positions are now idealized according to spacegroup data. In rare cases, this will cause re-indexing of atoms in the crystal. Site indexing conventions for certain reshaped systems may also change; use `position_to_site` for robust indexing of reshaped systems. Loading an mCIF as a chemical cell now employs a standardized Cartesian coordinate system, as would be obtained from `lattice_vectors`. Attempting to perform symmetry analysis on a crystal with a larger-than-standard chemical cell will error rather than give a wrong result.
* When loading a CIF or mCIF, the precision parameter `symprec` becomes optional (#413).
* Various enhancements to `minimize_energy!`. The return value becomes a struct that stores optimization statistics (#430). A small perturbation to the initial spin state breaks accidental symmetries (#442). Convergence to the local minimum becomes faster and more robust (#453).
* Fixes to `load_nxs` (#420).
* Add `interpolate` option to `plot_intensities`. Selecting `interpolate=true` will significantly reduce file sizes of PDF exports containing 2D heatmap data (#411).
* `set_spin_rescaling!` now expects a scaling factor for each symmetry-distinct sublattice (#444)).
* Introduce `set_spin_s_at!` to set the local quantum spin-s (#454).
`````

Users currently must manually craft prompts to generate content. This adds an AI-powered Content Planner that generates comprehensive topical authority maps—pillar topics, cluster articles, keywords, and publishing priorities—eliminating the strategic planning burden.

## Changes

### New PHP Class (`inc/class-content-planner.php`)
- `WritgoCMS_Content_Planner` handles topical map and detailed outline generation via AIMLAPI
- AJAX handlers for generating, saving, loading, and deleting content plans
- Plans stored in `writgocms_saved_content_plans` option with UUID keys

### Admin UI (`inc/admin-aiml-settings.php`)
- New "Content Planner" tab with inputs for niche, website type, target audience
- Results panel renders pillar content → cluster articles hierarchy
- Modal for saving plans with custom names

### Frontend (`assets/js/admin-aiml.js`, `assets/css/admin-aiml.css`)
- `renderTopicalMap()` displays AI-generated content structure with priority badges
- `renderContentPlan()` shows detailed article outlines with sections/subsections
- Save/load/export functionality for plans
- Dark mode support

## Usage

```
Settings → WritgoCMS AIML → Content Planner
1. Enter niche (e.g., "Digital Marketing")
2. Select website type
3. Click "Generate Topical Authority Map"
4. Click "Generate Detailed Plan" on any article for full outline
```

## Security
- All AJAX handlers verify nonces and check `edit_posts` capability
- HTML escaping via `escapeHtml()` and `escapeJsonAttr()` helpers
- Plan IDs use `wp_generate_uuid4()`

author: copilot
body:
Implements a FastAPI server at `http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions` that wraps all incoming chat completion requests with the Custodian Kernel Core Directive system message.

## Changes

- **`app/main.py`** - FastAPI app with `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint that injects Core Directive into all requests
- **`app/core_directive.py`** - Custodian Kernel Core Directive definition based on the inalienable right to pursue happiness
- **`app/models.py`** - Pydantic models with `Literal` type constraints for role validation
- **`tests/test_main.py`** - Test coverage for wrapping logic and API endpoints

## Core Directive

The Custodian Kernel Core Directive embodies the principle that every person has an equal, inalienable right to pursue happiness. The directive includes:

- **Core Principle**: The right is not a license for your pursuit, but a permanent limit on interfering with others' pursuits
- **Three Key Questions**: Does this infringe on anyone else's pursuit? Am I fucking anyone over? Am I making up a rule to force people to think like me?
- **Refusal → Explanation → Repair Pattern**: Framework for handling conflicts while respecting everyone's inalienable rights

## Behavior

- If no system message exists, prepends one with Core Directive
- If system message exists, prepends Core Directive to its content

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "gpt-3.5-turbo", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
```

Returns mock response indicating Core Directive was applied. Production use would forward wrapped messages to actual LLM API.

author: mathias82
body:
## PR Summary

This PR fixes an inconsistency in Quarkus dev mode where HTTP requests made during a failed application deployment could return **404 Not Found** instead of the expected **500 Internal Server Error**. The behavior was caused by the absence of a proper catch-all error handler during failed dev-mode startup, allowing unmatched routes to fall through Vert.x default routing.

## Related Issue

Fixes: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/50876

## Reproduction Steps

1. Create a Quarkus app with a failing injection (e.g. unresolved @ConfigProperty Boolean).
2. Run:
3. Send concurrent requests:

4. Observe mixed **404** and **500** responses.

## Expected vs Actual

| Scenario | Expected | Actual before PR | Actual after PR |
|---------|---------|-----------------|----------------|
| Dev mode deployment fails | Always 500 | Sometimes 404 | Always 500 |
| Browser access | Dev UI error | Works | Works |

## Fix Explanation

A final fallback route is now registered after the hot replacement handler, ensuring all requests during failed startup return a deterministic **500**:

```java
router.route().last().handler(rc -> {
 rc.response()
   .setStatusCode(500)
   .putHeader("Content-Type", "text/plain")
   .end("Dev mode startup failed – Application deployment did not complete successfully.");
});


No Breaking Changes
- Only affects dev mode during failed startup
- No API changes
- Dev UI behavior unchanged

Implements a real-time invisibility cloak effect using MediaPipe Selfie Segmentation and custom VFX for light-bending distortion.

## Core Components

- **`main.py`** - Application loop with PhantomCloak class
  - Background calibration via 30-frame running average (memory-efficient)
  - MediaPipe segmentation with landscape model for CPU performance
  - Two modes: ABSOLUTE (clean replacement) and PREDATOR (shimmer distortion)
  - Keyboard controls: `C` recalibrate, `M` mode switch, `+/-` refraction index, `Q` quit

- **`vfx_utils.py`** - VFX math and rendering
  - Edge detection (Canny) for mask boundaries
  - Displacement mapping via `cv2.remap` for light bending
  - Chromatic aberration via RGB channel shifting
  - Military-style HUD overlay with scanlines

- **`requirements.txt`** - opencv-python, mediapipe, numpy

## Usage

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py  # Default camera
python main.py 1  # Specific camera ID
```

The system captures a static background on startup, then replaces detected human pixels with that background in real-time. Predator mode adds animated edge distortion simulating optical refraction.

author: plajjan
body:
-9223372036854775808 is the most negative values of our int (i64). The standard lexer produces two tokens: - 9223372036854775808, which means this is constructed as an int64 type with the value 9223372036854775808 prefixed by the unary operator -. However, 9223372036854775808 is too large to be stored in a i64, so it fails.

We now parse negative integers into actual negative integers by combining the UMinus with the int value in the parser (after the lexer). Accordingly, CodeGen must now be able to produce negative bigint literals, which it does using a string C literal. Also adjusted type inference for large negative integers which now become bigint rather than int.

Added a new ints tests using codegen golden output to show the generated code.

Fixes #2545

# Hardware Module: Unified Hardware Services

## Summary

This PR introduces a unified hardware service architecture with REST APIs and CLI management for cameras, stereo cameras, PLCs, and sensors. The hardware module now provides consistent service-based access patterns, comprehensive test suites, and a command-line interface for service lifecycle management.

---

## Components

### 1. Camera Service

**API Service** (`api/cameras/`)
- MJPEG streaming with quality and FPS control
- Batch operations for multi-camera workflows
- Homography calibration and measurement endpoints

**New Backends**
- **GenICam Backend**: Full GenICam/GigE Vision support via Harvesters library
  - Matrix Vision CTI integration
  - Multicast streaming support
  - IP-based camera discovery
- **Basler Backend Enhancements**: Multicast streaming, exposure fallback patterns

**Homography Module** (`cameras/homography/`)
- Checkerboard-based calibration with rectangular square support
- Multi-view calibration for stitching long surfaces
- Real-world distance measurement from pixel coordinates
- Bounding box dimension measurement

### 2. Stereo Camera Service (New)

**API Service** (`api/stereo_cameras/`) - Port 8004
- Full REST API for Basler Stereo ace cameras
- Multi-component capture: intensity, disparity, and depth maps
- Point cloud generation with optional color data
- Configurable depth range, illumination, binning, and quality settings
- Batch capture operations
- Streaming endpoints for live depth data

**Core Implementation** (`stereo_cameras/`)
- `AsyncStereoCamera` - Async wrapper with context management
- `BaslerStereoAceBackend` - Native Basler Stereo ace support
- `StereoCapture` model with intensity, disparity, and point cloud data
- Setup scripts for Stereo ace SDK installation

### 3. PLC Service

**API Service** (`api/plcs/`) - Port 8003
- REST API for PLC connection management
- Tag read/write operations with type support
- Batch tag operations for efficient I/O
- Connection pooling and lifecycle management
- Backend discovery for Allen-Bradley.

---

## CLI

**Command**: `mindtrace-hw`

### Quick Start

```bash
# Install and verify
cd mindtrace/hardware && uv sync
mindtrace-hw --help

# Start camera service
mindtrace-hw camera start
mindtrace-hw camera start --open-docs      # Opens Swagger UI

# Start stereo camera service
mindtrace-hw stereo start

# Start PLC service
mindtrace-hw plc start

# Check all services
mindtrace-hw status

# Stop all services
mindtrace-hw stop
```

### Camera Commands

```bash
mindtrace-hw camera start [OPTIONS]
  --api-host TEXT      Host to bind (default: localhost)
  --api-port INTEGER   Port (default: 8002)
  --include-mocks      Include mock cameras for testing
  --open-docs          Open Swagger UI in browser

mindtrace-hw camera stop
mindtrace-hw camera status
mindtrace-hw camera test --list
mindtrace-hw camera test --config smoke_test
```

### Stereo Camera Commands

```bash
mindtrace-hw stereo start [OPTIONS]
  --api-host TEXT      Host to bind (default: localhost)
  --api-port INTEGER   Port (default: 8004)
  --open-docs          Open Swagger UI in browser

mindtrace-hw stereo stop
mindtrace-hw stereo status
```

### PLC Commands

```bash
mindtrace-hw plc start [OPTIONS]
  --api-host TEXT      Host to bind (default: localhost)
  --api-port INTEGER   Port (default: 8003)

mindtrace-hw plc stop
mindtrace-hw plc status
```

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `CAMERA_API_HOST` | localhost | Camera API host |
| `CAMERA_API_PORT` | 8002 | Camera API port |
| `STEREO_CAMERA_API_HOST` | localhost | Stereo camera API host |
| `STEREO_CAMERA_API_PORT` | 8004 | Stereo camera API port |
| `PLC_API_HOST` | localhost | PLC API host |
| `PLC_API_PORT` | 8003 | PLC API port |

---

## Test Suite

**Framework** (`test_suite/`)

A stress testing framework for hardware APIs with:
- Guaranteed cleanup via finally blocks
- Operation and scenario-level timeouts
- Metrics collection and performance analysis
- YAML-based test configuration

### Available Camera Tests

| Config | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `smoke_test` | Quick validation of basic operations |
| `capture_stress` | High-frequency capture stress testing |
| `multi_camera` | Concurrent multi-camera operations |
| `stream_stress` | Streaming stability and cleanup |
| `chaos_test` | Edge case discovery |
| `soak_test` | Long-duration stability |

### Running Tests

```bash
# List available tests
mindtrace-hw camera test --list

# Run smoke test
mindtrace-hw camera test --config smoke_test

# Run with verbose output
mindtrace-hw camera test --config capture_stress -v
```

---

## Unit Tests

856 tests covering:
- Camera backends (Basler, GenICam, OpenCV, Mock)
- Stereo camera models and backends
- Sensor backends and simulators
- API services and connection managers
- Homography calibration and measurement
- Configuration management

```bash
uv run pytest tests/unit/mindtrace/hardware -v
```

---

## API Endpoints Reference

### Camera API (8002)

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| GET | `/backends` | List available backends |
| GET | `/cameras` | List discovered cameras |
| POST | `/cameras/open` | Open camera by ID |
| POST | `/cameras/close` | Close camera |
| GET | `/cameras/{id}/status` | Get camera status |
| POST | `/cameras/capture` | Capture single image |
| POST | `/cameras/capture/hdr` | HDR capture |
| POST | `/cameras/stream/start` | Start MJPEG stream |
| POST | `/cameras/stream/stop` | Stop stream |
| POST | `/homography/calibrate` | Calibrate homography |
| POST | `/homography/measure` | Measure distance |

### Stereo Camera API (8004)

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| GET | `/backends` | List available backends |
| GET | `/cameras` | List stereo cameras |
| POST | `/cameras/open` | Open stereo camera |
| POST | `/cameras/close` | Close stereo camera |
| POST | `/cameras/capture` | Capture intensity + disparity |
| POST | `/cameras/pointcloud` | Generate point cloud |
| POST | `/cameras/configure` | Configure depth settings |

### PLC API (8003)

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| GET | `/backends` | List PLC backends |
| GET | `/plcs` | List discovered PLCs |
| POST | `/plcs/connect` | Connect to PLC |
| POST | `/plcs/disconnect` | Disconnect PLC |
| POST | `/tags/read` | Read tag value |
| POST | `/tags/write` | Write tag value |
| POST | `/tags/batch/read` | Batch read tags |

---

author: da2ce7
body:
### 1. `0cec63c` - Fix issue #64: parse 1e-15 exactly as 1/1000000000000000

**Problem:** When parsing very small numbers like `1e-15`, JavaScript's IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic causes precision errors. Specifically, `1/1e-15` evaluates to `999999999999999.9` instead of `1e15`, and `Math.floor()` then produces an incorrect result.

**Fix:** Added a relative epsilon check in `fullConversion()` for large values (`|q| > 1e10`). If the relative difference from the nearest integer is less than `1e-14` (~45× `Number.EPSILON`), the value is rounded to catch floating-point errors while preserving intentional fractional values.

**Files changed:** nerdamer.core.js, core.spec.js

---

### 2. `645d914` - Fix precision issues in multiply() and Frac.toDecimal()

**Two fixes:**
1. **`Frac.toDecimal()`:** Changed from `prec++` to `prec += 2` to provide proper rounding (one extra digit to round from, one for potential carry).

2. **`multiply()`:** Added proactive detection of when exact fraction arithmetic is needed by checking operand magnitudes *before* converting to decimal. This prevents precision loss for very small/large numbers that previously slipped through the zero-check fallback.

**Files changed:** nerdamer.core.js, LaTeX.spec.js, algebra.spec.js, core.spec.js

---

### 3. `071864e` - Add regression tests for precision underflow in multiply()

**Purpose:** Documents a precision bug where `1/7e19 * 7e19` returns `0.7` instead of `1` (a 30% error). The `multiply()` function uses `toDecimal()` with limited precision (21 digits), and when small fractions don't round to exactly zero, the fallback doesn't trigger, causing incorrect results.

This commit explains why naive fixes to issue #62 (decimal places off-by-one) break power calculations like `3.535401^3.535401`.

**Files changed:** core.spec.js

Implements automatic refresh logic to keep festival and drink data current during active festival periods.

Changes:
- Add timestamp tracking in BeerProvider (_lastDrinksRefresh, _lastFestivalsRefresh)
- Drinks data refreshes automatically after 1 hour of staleness
- Festivals list refreshes automatically after 24 hours of staleness
- App lifecycle observer in main.dart detects when app resumes from background
- refreshIfStale() method checks data age and refreshes only when needed
- Prevents redundant API calls when data is still fresh
- Maintains existing pull-to-refresh and manual retry functionality

This ensures users see up-to-date availability and new additions during the festival without manual intervention

Technical specification for a MIPT tutor marketplace platform with full API contract, database design, documentation, and website content.

## OpenAPI 3.0.3 Specification (`api/openapi.yaml`)
- Auth endpoints (register, login, JWT refresh)
- Tutor catalog with filters: subject, level, price range, rating, format, city, faculty
- Lesson request workflow (create → in_progress → completed)
- Reviews, favorites, in-app messaging
- Admin moderation endpoints
- Complete request/response schemas with validation

## PostgreSQL Schema (`db/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql`)
- 5 enums, 12 tables with proper FK relationships
- Denormalized `avg_rating` with auto-update trigger
- Performance indexes on filterable columns
- Seed data for subjects, levels, faculties

## Sample Data (`db/migrations/002_sample_data.sql`)
- Test users (admin, students, tutors)
- Sample profiles, lesson requests, reviews, messages

## Website Page Content (`content/pages.md`)
- Home page with hero section and popular subjects
- Tutor catalog with filter descriptions
- Tutor profile card template
- Registration and login pages
- Student and tutor dashboard layouts
- About us, contact, and FAQ pages
- Privacy policy and terms of service (brief versions)

## Documentation (`README.md`)
- API endpoint reference
- Schema documentation
- Getting started guide

GET /api/v1/tutors?subject_id=1&level=ege&price_max=2000&sort=rating_desc&page=1

Гость (неавторизованный пользователь)     * Просмотр главной страницы    * Просмотр каталога репетиторов и фильтров    * Просмотр карточки репетитора и отзывов    * Заполнение формы заявки (с последующей регистрацией или без, по решению)  2. Администратор     * Просмотр и управление пользователями    * Модерация анкет репетиторов (публикация/блокировка)    * Модерация отзывов    * Управление справочниками (предметы, категории и т.д.)    * Просмотр статистики (кол-во репетиторов, заявок и т.п.)  ---  ## 3. Авторизация и регистрация  * Регистрация по email + пароль (далее можно прикрутить соцсети). * Подтверждение email (опционально для MVP). * Авторизация по JWT (access + refresh). * Разделение ролей: STUDENT, TUTOR, ADMIN.  ### 3.2. Профиль ученика  * Поля: имя, фамилия, класс/курс, город, контакт (телега/телефон — по желанию). * Возможность видеть историю заявок, избранное, сообщения.  ### 3.3. Профиль репетитора  * Связь с пользователем. * Поля:    * ФИО   * Факультет/направление МФТИ   * Курс / выпуск   * О себе   * Цена за час   * Формат: онлайн/офлайн (+ город для офлайна)   * Предметы (с привязкой к справочнику)   * Уровни подготовки (ЕГЭ, ОГЭ, олимпиада, вуз, МФТИ-вступительные и т.п.)   * Ссылка на соцсети/Telegram (по желанию) * Статус: “на модерации / опубликован / отклонён / скрыт”.  ### 3.4. Каталог репетиторов  * Список карточек репетиторов с пагинацией, сортировками и фильтрами. * Базовый набор полей в карточке: фото, имя, предметы, цена, рейтинг, краткое “о себе”.  ### 3.5. Карточка репетитора  * Полный профиль + список предметов, уровней, стоимости. * Отзывы с оценкой. * Кнопка “Оставить заявку”. * Кнопка “Добавить в избранное” (для залогиненных).  ### 3.6. Заявки и бронирование  * Ученик оставляет заявку конкретному репетитору:    * предмет   * цель (ЕГЭ/контрольная/сессия/олимпиада и т.п.)   * уровень (класс/курс)   * комментарий   * желаемое время (произвольно текстом для MVP) * Репетитор может: принять / отклонить заявку, написать сообщение ученику. * Статусы: NEW, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, REJECTED.  ### 3.7. Избранное  * Сохранение репетиторов в список ученика. * Страница “Избранное” с карточками.  ### 3.9. author: moshpitcodes
body:
## Problem

GitHub CLI installation via apt repository consistently hangs during package download, causing Ansible playbook execution to stall indefinitely.

**Symptoms:**
- Installation hangs at "Update apt cache and install GitHub CLI" task
- Process stalls during package download from https://cli.github.com/packages
- No timeout or error - just indefinite hang
- Requires manual termination (Ctrl+C)

**Root Cause:**
- Unreliable network connectivity to GitHub CLI apt repository from WSL2
- Slow/timeout-prone HTTPS downloads through WSL2 networking
- apt repository metadata fetching issues on mounted Windows drives

## Solution

Replace apt repository installation with direct .deb package download from GitHub releases.

### Implementation

**Before (Repository-based):**
```yaml
- name: Update apt cache and install GitHub CLI
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    apt-get update
    apt-get install -y gh
  args:
    creates: /usr/bin/gh
  environment:
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND: noninteractive
```

**After (Direct Download):**
```yaml
- name: Download GitHub CLI deb package
  ansible.builtin.get_url:
    url: https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/download/v2.83.1/gh_2.83.1_linux_amd64.deb
    dest: /tmp/gh.deb
    mode: '0644'
    timeout: 60
  retries: 3
  delay: 5

- name: Install GitHub CLI from deb package
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    deb: /tmp/gh.deb
    state: present
  environment:
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND: noninteractive

- name: Clean up deb package
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: /tmp/gh.deb
    state: absent
```

## Benefits

✅ **Reliable installation** - Direct download from GitHub releases (proven stable)
✅ **Faster execution** - No apt repository metadata overhead
✅ **Better error handling** - 60s timeout with 3 retry attempts
✅ **WSL2 optimized** - Avoids known WSL2 apt repository issues
✅ **Cleaner process** - Downloads, installs, cleans up in clear steps
✅ **Pinned version** - Uses specific version (2.83.1) for consistency

## Trade-offs

**Advantages:**
- Much more reliable on WSL2
- Faster installation
- No dependency on apt repository availability
- Clear error messages if download fails

**Considerations:**
- Version is pinned (not auto-updating from repository)
- Repository tasks still configured (for potential future use)
- Requires internet access to GitHub releases

## Testing

- [x] Verified download works from GitHub releases
- [x] Confirmed .deb installation succeeds
- [x] Tested `gh --version` after installation
- [x] Validated cleanup of temporary file
- [x] Checked idempotency (skips if already installed)

## Migration Notes

After merging, GitHub CLI installation will work reliably:

```bash
# Pull latest changes
git pull origin main

# Install GitHub CLI
ANSIBLE_CONFIG=./ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook -K ansible/playbooks/main.yml --tags gh

# Verify installation
gh --version  # Should show: gh version 2.83.1
```

## Future Improvements

To keep GitHub CLI updated to latest version, we could:
1. Add a variable for version pinning
2. Use GitHub API to fetch latest release URL dynamically
3. Add a separate update task/playbook

For now, this provides a stable, working installation method.

## Summary

This PR enables the jib PR reviewer bot to make inline comments on specific lines of code and provide suggested fixes that can be committed directly from the GitHub UI.

### Changes Made

**1. Enhanced PR Review Workflow (`build_review_prompt`)**
- Instructs Claude to use GitHub MCP `pull_request_review_write` and `add_comment_to_pending_review` tools
- Provides step-by-step workflow:
  - Create a pending review
  - Add inline comments with line-specific feedback
  - Include suggested fixes using GitHub's `suggestion` code blocks
  - Submit the review with appropriate event type (COMMENT/APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES)

**2. Improved Comment Response Handling (`build_comment_prompt`)**
- Added workflow for handling inline review comments
- Enables responding to comment threads
- Includes instructions for applying and committing suggested changes
- Maintains proper branch verification to avoid cross-contamination

### Capabilities Enabled

✅ **Inline comments** - jib can now comment on specific lines of code during reviews
✅ **Suggested fixes** - Reviewers can commit suggestions directly via GitHub UI
✅ **Comment responses** - jib can respond to inline comments from human reviewers
✅ **Commit suggestions** - jib can apply and commit suggested changes when appropriate

### How It Works

When jib receives a PR review request, it will:
1. Create a pending review using GitHub MCP
2. Analyze the diff and add inline comments on specific lines
3. Provide suggested fixes in markdown code blocks (```suggestion)
4. Submit the complete review

When jib receives inline comments from reviewers, it can:
1. Read and understand the feedback
2. Respond in the comment thread
3. Apply suggested changes if appropriate
4. Commit and push changes to the PR branch

author: scetrov
body:
Summary
- Add a CI workflow to enforce ADR naming and immutability, and a Node validation script.

Changes
- `.github/workflows/adr-guard.yml`: Runs on PRs/pushes that touch `docs/adrs/**`. Uses `.nvmrc` for Node (via setup-node), corepack for pnpm, and reads `adr-override` label on PRs.
- `scripts/validate_adrs.js`: Validates ADRs with rules:
  - Filename regex `^\d{4}-[a-z0-9-]+\.md$`
  - Header first line `# ADR <ID>:` must match filename ID
  - No edits/renames/deletes to historical ADRs unless PR label `adr-override` is present
  - `TEMPLATE.md` exempt
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: Documented ADR guard rules and override procedure.

Why
- Align with ADR immutability guidance (ADR 0001) and DevSecOps change control (ADR 0007). Prevent silent edits to historical decisions.

Validation
- Local smoke test: `node scripts/validate_adrs.js` passes when no ADR changes present.
- Separate PR (#13) demonstrates failing scenario.

Backout
- Revert workflow or script if it blocks legitimate changes; otherwise use `adr-override` label for rare exceptions.

body:
### **User description** ## Summary - Fixes bug where saving NSFW figures failed with 500 error - Backend now extracts `mfcAuth` from request body in `createFigure` and `updateFigure` - Adds smart scraping: only scrapes MFC if fields are actually missing - Passes `mfcAuth` to scraper when scraping is needed ## Root Cause The backend was: 1. Not extracting `mfcAuth` from requests (frontend was sending it correctly) 2. Re-scraping MFC on every save, even when all fields were already populated 3. The redundant scrape failed for NSFW content because no auth was passed ## Changes - `src/controllers/figureController.ts`: - `createFigure`: Extract `mfcAuth`, check if scrape needed, pass auth if scraping - `updateFigure`: Extract `mfcAuth`, check if scrape needed, pass auth if scraping ## Test Plan - [x] All 400 existing tests pass - [x] TypeScript compiles without errors - [ ] Manual test: Save NSFW figure with auth cookies → should succeed - [ ] Manual test: Save figure with all fields filled → should skip scrape ___ ### **PR Type** Bug fix, Enhancement ___ ### **Description** - Extract `mfcAuth` from request body in both `createFigure` and `updateFigure` - Add smart scraping logic to only scrape MFC when required fields are missing - Pass `mfcAuth` to scraper to enable NSFW content access - Add debug logging to track scrape decisions and auth availability ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Request with mfcAuth"] --> B["Extract mfcAuth from body"] B --> C["Check if fields missing"] C -->|Missing fields| D["Scrape MFC with auth"] C -->|All fields present| E["Skip scrape"] D --> F["Merge scraped data"] E --> F F --> G["Save figure"] ```

File Walkthrough
Relevant files
Bug fix
figureController.ts
Add mfcAuth extraction and conditional scraping logic       
src/controllers/figureController.ts
  • Extract mfcAuth parameter from request body in both createFigure and
    updateFigure handlers
  • Implement smart scraping logic that checks if required fields are
    missing before calling scrapeDataFromMFC
  • Pass mfcAuth as second parameter to scrapeDataFromMFC function to
    enable NSFW content scraping
  • Add debug console logging to track when scrapes are performed vs
