## Description

This PR adds comprehensive GitHub Actions workflows for CI/CD, fixes all test failures discovered during workflow testing, and improves test architecture to respect layered boundaries. All 511 tests now pass, and workflows are verified locally using `act`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update (changes to documentation only)
- [x] Refactoring (code changes that neither fix bugs nor add features)
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [x] Test updates

## Changes Made

### CI/CD Workflows Added
- **CI Workflow** (`ci.yml`): Format check, Clippy lint, Build check across platforms (ubuntu, macos, windows)
- **Test Workflow** (`test.yml`): Unit tests with cargo-nextest, doc tests
- **Coverage Workflow** (`coverage.yml`): Code coverage reporting with codecov
- **Security Workflow** (`security.yml`): Automated dependency security audits (scheduled + manual trigger)
- **Integration Workflow** (`integration.yml`): End-to-end CLI testing with standard and SQLite backend tests
- **Release Workflow** (`release.yml`): Manual release trigger with automated version detection from Cargo.toml

### Test Fixes
- Fixed step renumbering bug in scenario deletion (decrement instead of increment)
- Fixed category change file moving logic (delete old files before saving to new location)
- Fixed permission test for Docker/root environments (handle cases where permission restrictions don't apply)
- Fixed doc tests for private module examples (marked as `ignore` since modules are private)
- Re-enabled SQLite backend test (was incorrectly marked `#[ignore]` - works fine with same runner instance)

### Test Architecture Improvements
- Removed direct repository access from interactive CLI tests
- Tests now verify behavior through `InteractiveRunner` interface only (no boundary violations)
- Added meaningful assertions instead of weak `is_ok()` checks
- Simplified initialization tests to avoid checking internal state (Config, ProjectController)
- All tests respect layered architecture boundaries

### Integration Tests Refactored
- Replaced outdated 20-test suite with focused test flows:
  - **Standard CLI Test**: 7 tests covering init, actors, use cases, conditions, references, file generation, status
  - **SQLite Backend Test**: 3 tests for database initialization, creation, and persistence
- Updated commands to match current CLI structure (`actor create-system`, etc.)
- Removed interactive mode test (would require `expect`/`pexpect` for real prompt testing)

### Release Workflow Improvements
- Changed to manual trigger only (`workflow_dispatch` instead of tag push)
- Automatically reads version from `Cargo.toml` (no manual version input needed)
- Removed unnecessary code change detection logic
- Simplified publish step
- 
## Testing

### Test Strategy

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Tested on multiple platforms (if applicable)

This PR introduces optimized implementation of `PartitionJobHandler` and `MergeJobHandler`.

- `PartitionJobHandler`: now partitions input file more efficiently by utilizing the fact that input file is already sorted, which results in speedup of around 3 times.
- `MergeJobHandler`: do comparison directly instead of creating `Record` object for every 100 byte frames. This reduces GC overhead caused by creating excessive short-lived objects.

body: Idea behind lightweight kernel asserts it to make a hang that would tt-triage detect. These asserts use only `ebreak` after `if`, so they are really lightweight on the kernel code. On the other hand, they don't provide too much information. To accommodate that, tt-triage script for lightweight asserts will show callstack for them (helping users see exact file/line that hit the assert). Sample script output: Since lots of information is available on the stack, we can open gdb client that is connected to the risc core that hit the assert (it if is not ncrisc). Since gdb might be too advanced for most of the users, we are [experimenting with argument and local variable extraction on the stack itself](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-exalens/pull/733). This would maybe help users understand problem that assert line is showing.

author: technickai
body:
## Summary

Makes Clerk authentication optional, allowing the app to build and run without Clerk keys configured. This supports git worktrees, forked repos, and local development while maintaining full production auth functionality.

## Key Changes

**New Components:**
- `OptionalClerkProvider` - Conditionally wraps app with ClerkProvider based on key presence
- `useOptionalUser` - Safe wrapper around Clerk's `useUser` hook that works without keys
- `OptionalUserButton` - User button that only renders when Clerk is configured

**Updated Components:**
- `app/layout.tsx` - Uses OptionalClerkProvider instead of ClerkProvider directly
- `app/connect/page.tsx` - Uses OptionalUserButton for conditional auth UI
- `components/ui/greeting.tsx` - Uses useOptionalUser hook
- `components/ui/connect-cta.tsx` - Uses useOptionalUser hook
- `lib/env.ts` - Removed Clerk key warning (now handled gracefully)

## Scenarios Supported

### Without Clerk Keys
- ✅ Build succeeds
- ✅ App runs normally
- ❌ Auth-protected features fail at runtime (expected)
- Perfect for: git worktrees, forks, local non-auth development

### With Clerk Keys
- ✅ Build succeeds
- ✅ Full authentication enabled
- ✅ All features work normally
- No behavioral change from before

## Testing

**Build validation:**
- ✅ Builds successfully without Clerk keys
- ✅ Builds successfully with Clerk keys
- ✅ Type checking passes
- ✅ Linting passes
- ✅ All tests pass (96 tests)

**Use case validation:**
- ✅ Git worktrees can share env from main repo or run without keys
- ✅ Forked repos can explore codebase without Clerk setup
- ✅ Production deployments require Clerk keys for auth features

## Implementation Pattern

This follows the mcp-hubby pattern where environment variables are:
- Optional at import time (supports builds without full config)
- Validated at point of use via `assertEnv()` when actually needed

The OptionalClerkProvider pattern can be applied to other optional services (analytics, monitoring, etc.) following the same approach.

## Documentation

Updated `.env.example` with clear instructions about optional Clerk setup and the supported scenarios.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> Makes Clerk authentication optional and refactors app to use an internal user context with conditional Clerk provider and UI.
> 
> - **Auth & Providers**:
>   - Add `lib/auth/optional-clerk-provider` to enable/disable Clerk based on `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
>   - Add `lib/auth/user-context` (`UserProvider`, `useUserContext`) with mock fallback when Clerk keys are absent.
>   - Replace direct `ClerkProvider`/`useUser` usage with new providers/hooks in `app/layout.tsx` and dependent components.

## Purpose / Description
The `resetAnkiDroidDirectory` method signature was changed in PR #2, removing the optional `directory` parameter. This broke the call in `DatabaseErrorDialog.kt:527` which passes two arguments.

## Fixes
* Fixes feedback from [PR #2 review](https://github.com/7se7en72025/Anki-Android/pull/2#discussion_r2574600952)

## Approach
Restored the original method signature with the optional `directory` parameter:

```kotlin
fun resetAnkiDroidDirectory(
    context: Context,
    directory: File = getDefaultAnkiDroidDirectory(context),
)
```

This allows both calling patterns:
- `resetAnkiDroidDirectory(context)` — uses default directory
- `resetAnkiDroidDirectory(context, directory)` — uses specified directory (as used by `DatabaseErrorDialog.kt`)

## How Has This Been Tested?
Code review verified the signature matches both the original implementation and existing call sites.

author: riyam224
body:
# 🔥 PR: Complete Authentication + Security Layer (Biometrics, Sessions, App Lock, Root Detection, Screenshot Protection)

This PR introduces the full authentication + security system for the FinTech app.
It’s the foundation for everything we’ll build next, so I focused on clean architecture, predictable flows, and making all security features work together smoothly.

---

# ⭐ Overview

This PR includes:

* Email/Password authentication (with Firebase)
* Fingerprint + Face ID flows
* Secure session lifecycle (with inactivity timeout)
* App Lock on resume
* Root/Jailbreak detection
* Screenshot/recording protection
* Background blur (iOS + Android)
* Updated protected routing using GoRouter
* Improved dependency injection structure
* Unit tests for domain + auth logic
* Android & iOS demo videos

---

# 🔐 1. Authentication

**What’s implemented:**

* Email/password login
* User registration with stronger validation rules
* Cleaned and refactored `AuthCubit`
* Firebase authentication integrated in the data layer
* Full biometric flow (Fingerprint on Android, Face ID on iOS)

### 🔁 Auth Flow

```
Splash
 ├─ First-time → Onboarding → Login
 └─ Returning → Login
Login Success → Biometric Verify → Home
```

### Validation improvements

* **Email** → trimmed + normalized
* **Password** → upper, lower, digit, special character
* **Name** → supports spaces, hyphens, apostrophes
* **Phone** → trimmed + required

---

# 🛡️ 2. Security Architecture

### Session Manager

It stores:

* userId
* token
* refreshToken (placeholder)
* session start time
* last activity

And handles:

* validity checks
* sessionStateStream
* activity updates
* session timeout

This is fully integrated with the router redirects and app lifecycle events in `main.dart`.

---

### App Lock System

* Automatically locks the app after inactivity
* On resume → user must unlock using biometrics
* `/app-lock` route included
* Works together with the session manager

---

### Root / Jailbreak Detection

* Detects unsafe environments
* Navigates to `/root-warning`
* User can exit or continue “at your own risk”

---

### Screenshot & Recording Blocking

* **Android** → `FLAG_SECURE`
* **iOS** → blur overlay
* Enabled/disabled automatically per-route via `AppRouteObserver`

Protected routes:

* home
* market
* portfolio
* coin details
* transactions
* profile
* buy/sell

---

### Background Blur

Added `SecureApplication` so the UI blurs whenever the app goes background.

---

# 🧭 3. Navigation (GoRouter)

New / updated routes:

* `/splash`
* `/onboarding`
* `/login`
* `/register`
* `/biometric-setup`
* `/biometric-verify`
* `/biometric-success`
* `/app-lock`
* `/root-warning`
* `/home` (protected)
* `/market`
* `/portfolio`
* `/settings`
* `/profile`

Protected routes now use:

```dart
if (!isProtected) return null;
if (!sessionManager.isSessionValid()) return AppRoutes.login;
```

---

# ⚙️ 4. Dependency Injection

Reorganized the DI file to make it cleaner and easier to maintain.

For testing, I added simple in-memory/no-op implementations for:

* secure storage
* biometrics
* screenshot prevention
* root detection
* session manager

This prevents platform services from breaking tests.

---

# 🧪 5. Testing

### Passed unit tests:

* Login use case
* Register use case
* Validators
* AuthCubit
* BiometricVerifyCubit (duplicate-call handling)

### Skipped (hardware / platform dependent):

* real biometrics
* real root detection
* real screenshot prevention
* app lock timers

---

# 🎥 6. Demo Videos

I attached short videos to make the review easier.

### 📱 Android Demo

(Fingerprint, login, app lock, protected routes)

![pr_ready](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df6eabdc-4596-455a-90c8-ee1584eff118)



### 🍏 iOS Demo

(Face ID, background blur, protected navigation)


![auth_ios_compressed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b72c14a-fef4-43ef-a3ac-68779f08fd37)


# 📚 Documentation Added

* `docs/AUTH_FLOW.md`
* `docs/SECURITY.md`
* `docs/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md`
* `docs/SPLASH_ONBOARDING.md`

These document the flows and security logic in detail.

---


# 🙏 Request for Review

Please review:

* Architecture decisions
* Security flows
* Routing protections
* Session/AppLock behavior
* Biometric UX

I’m open to adjusting anything based on your feedback.

author: chrislusf
body:
This PR fixes the Helm install issue described in #163 by updating the GitHub Actions workflow for publishing Helm charts.

## Changes Made

- Modified `.github/workflows/helm_chart_release.yml` to create chart releases using the chart version tag format (`seaweedfs-operator-{version}`)
- Updated the Helm repo index update to use the correct download URLs pointing to the chart-specific releases
- Added proper step ID for the chart version setting to enable output usage

## Problem

The original workflow was uploading chart packages to app version releases (e.g., 1.0.6) but the index.yaml was pointing to non-existent URLs, causing 404 errors when users tried to install via Helm.

## Solution

By creating dedicated releases for each chart version with the format `seaweedfs-operator-{chart_version}`, the download URLs in index.yaml will always be correct and point to existing assets.

## Testing

To fix the existing broken index.yaml entry for version 0.1.5:
1. Go to the Actions tab in the repository
2. Run the "helm: publish charts" workflow manually with tag "1.0.6"
3. This will create the missing `seaweedfs-operator-0.1.5` release with the chart package
4. The index.yaml will be updated with the correct URL

Future releases will automatically have correct URLs.

Fixes #163

body:
## Summary

Enhances the fragment index-based peptide search engine with comprehensive open-search modification discovery capabilities and demonstrates quality filtering workflows using existing OpenMS classes.

### Modification Discovery Engine (`OpenSearchModificationAnalysis`)
- **Delta mass histogram**: Bins precursor mass shifts, counts PSMs per bin, tracks unique peptides and charge states
- **PTM mapping**: Maps delta masses to known modifications via `ModificationsDB` with capped tolerance
- **Residue frequency analysis**: Per-delta-mass amino acid composition to help localize modifications
- **Structured results**: `DeltaMassEntry`, `PTMEntry`, `DeltaMassStatistics`, `PTMStatistics`, `OpenSearchAnalysisResult`
- **TSV export**: `writeDeltaMassStatistics()` and `writePTMStatistics()` for downstream analysis

### Search Engine Enhancements (`PeptideSearchEngineFIAlgorithm`)
- **In-memory search overloads**: `search(MSExperiment, FASTAEntries, ...)` and `searchWithModificationAnalysis()` for programmatic use without file I/O
- **`SearchResult` struct**: Bundles exit code, open-search flag, peptide IDs, protein IDs, and modification analysis in one return value
- **Formatted logging**: Tables of top PTMs and unknown delta masses for interactive discovery

### FDR and Score Filtering Workflows (tests only, no new C++ code)
- **FDR-based**: Search with `decoys=true` → `FalseDiscoveryRate::apply()` → `IDFilter::filterHitsByScore()` at 5% FDR → `removeDecoyHits` → standalone `OpenSearchModificationAnalysis`
- **Score-based**: Search without decoys → `IDFilter::filterHitsByScore()` on raw ln(hyperscore) → standalone modification analysis
- Both workflows verified in C++ and Python tests

### Python Bindings
- Full autowrap `.pxd` bindings for all new classes and result types
- 5 end-to-end Python tests covering open search discovery, closed search, empty input, FDR filtering, and score filtering

## Test plan
- [x] C++ unit tests: `PeptideSearchEngineFIAlgorithm_test` (8 sections all pass)
- [x] C++ unit tests: `OpenSearchModificationAnalysis_test` (passes)
- [x] Python tests: `test_modification_discovery.py` (5 tests, all pass)

# Sistema de Votação com Real-Time Updates

## 📋 Descrição

Esta PR implementa um sistema completo de votação com as seguintes funcionalidades:

- ✅ Criação e visualização de votações
- ✅ Sistema de votação (votar/cancelar voto)
- ✅ Encerramento de votações pelos criadores
- ✅ Atualização em tempo real usando Socket.IO
- ✅ Interface responsiva e intuitiva
- ✅ Cobertura completa de testes (191 testes passando)

## 🚀 Principais Funcionalidades

### 1. Sistema de Votação

- **Vote em opções**: Usuários autenticados podem votar em qualquer opção
- **Cancele seu voto**: Pode cancelar e votar novamente a qualquer momento
- **Visualização de resultados**: Percentuais e contagem de votos em tempo real
- **Indicação visual**: Marca clara da opção em que você votou

### 2. Gerenciamento de Polls

- **Encerrar votação**: Criadores podem encerrar suas votações
- **Status visual**: Badges indicando se a votação está aberta ou encerrada
- **Página de detalhes**: Visualização completa com todas as opções e estatísticas

### 3. Real-Time Updates com Socket.IO

- **Conexão WebSocket**: Atualização instantânea quando alguém vota
- **Otimizado**: Socket conecta apenas na página de detalhes (não na home)
- **Reconexão automática**: Mantém conexão estável com retry automático
- **Gerenciamento de salas**: Cada poll tem sua própria sala para updates isolados

### 4. Interface e UX

- **Design consistente**: Dark theme com purple accent
- **Responsivo**: Funciona perfeitamente em desktop e mobile
- **Feedback visual**: Loading states e toasts para todas as ações
- **Prevenção de cliques múltiplos**: Lógica para evitar cliques acidentais em botões

## 🔧 Mudanças Técnicas

### Backend API Alignment

- Atualizados tipos para corresponder à estrutura do backend
- `status: 'OPEN' | 'CLOSED'` em vez de enum
- `votedOption: string | null` para indicar voto do usuário
- `creator.id` como string para compatibilidade

### Novos Serviços

```typescript
// Vote Service
createVote(data: CreateVoteDto): Promise<void>
deleteVote(pollId: string): Promise<void>

// Poll Service
closePoll(pollId: string): Promise<void>

// Socket Service
connect(): Promise<Socket>
joinPoll(pollId: string): Promise<void>
leavePoll(): void
onPollUpdated(callback): void
```

### Novos Componentes

- **PollDetailsPage**: Página completa de votação (409 linhas)
  - Renderização de opções com barras de progresso
  - Lógica de votação e cancelamento
  - Integração com Socket.IO
  - Controles de encerramento para owners

### Melhorias na HomePage

- Botão de encerrar votação nos cards
- Verificação de ownership para mostrar controles
- Badges de status (aberta/encerrada)
- Prevenção de navegação ao clicar em botões internos

## 🧪 Testes

**191 testes passando em 17 suites**

### Novos Arquivos de Teste

- `tests/polldetails.test.tsx` (~50 testes)
  - Renderização e carregamento
  - Sistema de votação completo
  - Encerramento de polls
  - Validações de permissões
  - Estados de loading e erro

- `tests/voteservice.test.ts` (~30 testes)
  - Criação de votos
  - Cancelamento de votos
  - Tratamento de erros
  - Edge cases

- `tests/__mocks__/socketService.ts`
  - Mock completo do socket service
  - Suporte a async/await

### Testes Atualizados

- `tests/homepage.test.tsx`: Adicionados testes de close poll
- Todos os testes adaptados para nova estrutura da API

## 📊 Commits

Esta branch contém 19 commits organizados por tipo:

### Features (7)

- `feat: add vote types for voting system`
- `feat: implement vote service with create and delete endpoints`
- `feat: add userId to auth context and persist on login`
- `feat: implement poll details page with voting functionality`
- `feat: add close poll functionality to homepage`

### Refactors (5)

It adds comprehensive test coverage for the new endpoint and updates the frontend to use an actor-based state machine for profile loading and saving, with improved user feedback through notifications.

**Backend: Profile Retrieval API**

* Added `getProfile` method to the repository (`profile.repository.interface.ts`, `profile.repository.postgres.ts`), service (`profile.service.ts`), and API handler (`profile-api-handler.ts`), allowing retrieval of a user's profile or `null` if not found. body:
## **User description** ### SUMMARY This PR fixes Issue #35347, where the Stop button in Chart and Dashboard views did not actually stop running queries on Trino and other databases. **Previously:** - The stop button in the Explore/Chart view was not wired to the backend cancellation logic. - Chart queries were effectively stateless from the perspective of cancellation and did not carry query_id / client tracking information used by the backend to kill queries. - As a result, clicking Stop, closing the tab, refreshing the page, or navigating away would still leave the query running on the database, consuming unnecessary compute resources. **This PR:** - Adds client and query tracking for chart queries so they carry the necessary identifiers for cancellation. - Wires the chart stop button to a new backend API endpoint that uses the same query-killing logic already used by SQL Lab. - Ensures that when a user clicks Stop in Chart view, a cancellation request is sent to the backend, which then kills the corresponding running query on the database. **Key changes include:** *Frontend:* - `superset-frontend/src/components/Chart/chartAction.js` - `superset-frontend/src/components/Chart/chartReducer.ts` - `superset-frontend/src/explore/components/ExploreViewContainer/index.jsx` - `superset-frontend/src/explore/exploreUtils/index.js` - `superset-frontend/src/explore/types.ts` These changes add client/query tracking to chart queries and connect the Stop button to the new cancellation API. *Backend:* - `superset/charts/schemas.py` - `superset/common/query_context.py` - `superset/common/query_context_factory.py` - `superset/common/query_context_processor.py` - `superset/models/core.py` - `superset/models/helpers.py` These changes ensure that chart queries are created with client/query identifiers and that the backend can locate and cancel the corresponding running query. Behaviorally, there are no breaking changes: the Stop button now behaves as expected by users (similar to SQL Lab), and no existing functionality is regressed. ### BEFORE/AFTER SCREENSHOTS OR ANIMATED GIF No visual UI changes. The Stop button remains the same visually; only its behavior is corrected (it now kills the backend query). **Behavioral demonstration:** - **Before:** Clicking Stop in Chart view would stop the frontend loading indicator, but the query continued running in the database (e.g., Trino), wasting resources. - **After:** Clicking Stop in Chart view sends a cancellation request to the backend, which kills the query in the database. The query transitions to a cancelled/killed state (e.g., `USER ERROR: ADMINISTRATIVELY KILLED` in Trino). ### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS 1. Set up Superset with Trino (or another supported DB where you can see running queries). 2. Start Superset and log in. 3. Go to **Explore / Create Chart** and configure a chart that triggers a long-running query (e.g., a heavy query against Trino). 4. Open the Trino UI (or the database's query monitoring UI) to observe running queries. 5. In Chart view, run the chart and confirm the query appears as running in Trino. 6. Click the **Stop** button in Chart view. 7. Verify in the Trino UI that: - The query is cancelled, and - It transitions to an error such as `USER ERROR: ADMINISTRATIVELY KILLED` (or the equivalent cancellation message for your database). 8. Repeat the above steps from a Dashboard that contains a chart to confirm that stopping from the Dashboard view also cancels the underlying query. **Additionally:** - Run the existing test suite to ensure no regressions: - `pytest` (backend) - `npm test` / `pnpm test` (frontend), as appropriate for the repo setup. - Confirm that SQL Lab query cancellation behavior remains unchanged and still works as expected (regression check). ### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION - [x] Has associated issue: Fixes #35347 - [ ] Required feature flags: - [ ] Changes UI - [ ] Includes DB Migration (follow approval process in [SIP-59](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/13351)) - [ ] Migration is atomic, supports rollback & is backwards-compatible - [ ] Confirm DB migration upgrade and downgrade tested - [ ] Runtime estimates and downtime expectations provided - [x] Introduces new feature or API - [ ] Removes existing feature or API **Additional notes:** - No new external dependencies are introduced. - No performance concerns identified; cancelling queries should reduce unnecessary resource usage. - No DB migrations are required. - The change reuses the existing SQL Lab query cancellation mechanism, ensuring consistent behavior across SQL Lab and Explore/Chart views. Contributors: - [Vab-170](https://github.com/Vab-170) - [ssadras](https://github.com/ssadras) - [X-arshiya-X](https://github.com/X-arshiya-X) - [Infernashwin](https://githu.com/Infernashwin) ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Make the Explore chart Stop button cancel running database queries ### What Changed - Clicking Stop in Explore now cancels the underlying database query, not just the in-flight HTTP request - Each chart query now includes a client-generated id so the backend can track and stop that specific query - Query cancellation is more robust across databases, reducing cases where a stopped chart leaves work running in the database - If the backend fails to stop a query, the UI shows a clear toast error instead of failing silently ### Impact `✅ Chart queries can be reliably cancelled from Explore` `✅ Fewer abandoned long-running chart queries after clicking Stop or navigating away` `✅ Lower database load from cancelled or abandoned chart runs`

author: camdot
body:
## About the PR
Fixes puddles and footsteps getting stuck and becoming unmoppable. They'd show 0 units when examined but wouldn't disappear. mopping did nothing, and the only fix was space cleaner.

## Why / Balance
Puddles should actually disappear when they evaporate, and you should be able to mop them properly.

## Technical details

Two issues in PuddleSystem.Evaporation.cs:

1. When evaporation removed liquid, it modified the solution directly without calling UpdateChemicals(). No events fired, so the puddle never got added to the deletion queue.

2. UpdateEvaporation() returned early if the evaporation component already existed, without ever checking if it should be removed. So mixed liquids (water + blood) would get stuck - water evaporates but the component stays attached doing nothing.

The mopping system checks "if (volume <= 0) return",  basically "nothing to mop here"

Fix: Call UpdateChemicals() after evaporation, and change UpdateEvaporation() to actually remove the component when there's no evaporatables left.

author: osomalley
body:
## Description Alongside the rest of the initialization for `subpixel_radiance`, an empty `MediumStack` is initialized. Its behavior is conceptually similar to the existing `CompositeBSDF`. Media are stored in a statically allocated `char` pool, with pointers maintained in `mediums[MaxMediums]`. In processing medium closures, either `HomogeneousMedium` or `EmptyMedium` are inserted into the medium stack. There is a simple priority handling scheme that will shuffle the incumbent medium pointers to give high priority mediums lower indices. They both inherit from a shared CRTP interface, `Medium`. When processing BSDF closures, intersections with `MxDielectric` or `MxGeneralizedSchlick` may only be added when `priority < current_priority` or are both 0 (the precious priority). Attached to the `MediumStack`, an `integrate` method transmittance samples each medium and scatters using the phase function of the highest priority medium. As of now, only `HenyeyGreenstein` is implemented and inherits from `BSDF`. With this being both a sizable update and my first commit to the project, I’m more than happy to iterate on this. ### Tests `render-mx-medium-glass`, `render-mx-medium-vdf`, `render-mx-medium-anisotropic` with OptiX references of the latter two. The images for `render-mx-generalized-schlick-glass` and `render-mx-dielectric-schlick-glass` have been updated as well.

body:
The unified importer in `scripts/importer/` was failing because language and country importers queried the legacy database with incorrect schema (expecting `code` column that doesn't exist). This caused a cascade: languages failed → projects failed on FK constraint (`language_id: 'eng'`) → all 4,385 items skipped because dependencies not found.

## Verification

The fix was already applied in commit 61d09b4 (PR #545). This PR confirms:

- **Languages/Countries**: Now load from JSON files (`database/seeders/data/languages.json`, `countries.json`) instead of legacy DB queries
- **Projects**: Can now create with `language_id: 'eng'` because language record exists
- **Items**: Can now resolve dependencies (context, collection, partner) and import successfully

```typescript
// Before: Queried legacy DB with wrong column names
const languages = await this.context.legacyDb.query<LegacyLanguage>(
  'SELECT * FROM mwnf3.langs ORDER BY code'  // ❌ 'code' doesn't exist
);

// After: Loads from production JSON file
const languagesPath = join(__dirname, '../../../../../database/seeders/data/languages.json');
const languages = JSON.parse(readFileSync(languagesPath, 'utf-8'));
```

## Test Results

- All 70 unit tests pass
- TypeScript compiles clean
- Linting passes
- Import order verified: default-context → languages → countries → projects → partners → items

<issue_title>Fixes for scripts/importer</issue_title>
<issue_description># Critical Fixes Required for Unified Importer

## Context

The new unified importer in `scripts/importer/` (implemented in PRs metanull/inventory-app#541, metanull/inventory-app#542, metanull/inventory-app#543 per issue metanull/inventory-app#540) is currently non-functional and produces numerous errors. This issue details all required fixes to achieve parity with the working `scripts/legacy-import/sql-import-v2.ts` importer.

## Test Results

Latest run: `import-2025-11-30T19-46-32-533Z.log`
- **Phase 0 (Reference Data)**: 1 imported, 0 skipped, 4 errors
- **Phase 1 (Projects and Partners)**: 267 imported, 0 skipped, 57 errors  
- **Phase 2 (Items)**: 0 imported, 4385 skipped, 0 errors
- **Total**: 268 imported, 4385 skipped, **61 errors**

## Critical Issues

### 1. ❌ Items Incorrectly Marked as "Skipped" Instead of Being Imported

**Observation:**
```
Starting Objects...
Completed Objects: 0 imported, 3715 skipped, 0 errors (1.03s)

Starting Monuments...
Completed Monuments: 0 imported, 670 skipped, 0 errors (0.20s)
```

**Root Cause:**
All 4,385 items (objects + monuments) are being skipped, but none are being imported. This suggests:
- False positive in existence checking
- Items already exist in database from previous failed run
- Or skip logic is incorrectly triggered

**Location:**
- `scripts/importer/src/importers/phase-01/object-importer.ts`
- `scripts/importer/src/importers/phase-01/monument-importer.ts`
- Likely in `BaseImporter.entityExists()` method

**Investigation Needed:**
1. Check if items are being incorrectly detected as existing
2. Verify backward compatibility tracking between importer runs
3. Ensure database is properly wiped before import

---

### 2. ⚠️ Architecture Gap: Missing Legacy Database Adapter

**Problem:**
The new importer's `ImportContext.legacyDb` interface expects:
```typescript
interface ILegacyDatabase {
  query<T>(sql: string, params?: unknown[]): Promise<T[]>;
  // ...
}
```

But the legacy database schema has different table names and structures than what the queries expect:
- Legacy: `mwnf3.langs` → New queries expect: `languages` with `code` column
- Legacy: `mwnf3.countries` → New queries expect: `countries` with `code` column
- Legacy: `mwnf3.langnames` → New queries expect: correct table/column names

**Working Approach (old importer):**
- Queries legacy database with correct schema: `SELECT * FROM mwnf3.langs`
- No assumptions about modern schema structure
- Direct SQL queries matching actual legacy table structure

**Fix Required:**
Create a proper legacy database query layer that:
1. Uses actual legacy table names (`langs`, `countries`, `projects`, etc.) - Mapping table for legacy IDs and new model's IDs exist: scripts/importers/src/utils/code-mappings.ts
2. Maps legacy columns to expected interface types
3. Handles schema differences between legacy and new databases

---

### 3. ⚠️ Missing Database Configuration

**Problem:**
The CLI tool in `scripts/importer/src/cli/import.ts` creates a `LegacyDatabase` class inline with basic config, but:
- No documentation about required environment variables
- No validation that legacy database is accessible
- Connection errors are silent/unclear

**Environment Variables Expected:**
```
LEGACY_DB_HOST
LEGACY_DB_PORT
LEGACY_DB_USER
LEGACY_DB_PASSWORD
LEGACY_DB_DATABASE
```

**Fix Required:**
1. Document required environment variables in README
2. Add connection validation on startup
3. Provide clear error messages if legacy DB is unreachable

---

### 4. ⚠️ Sample Collection Not Implemented

**Missing Feature:**
Old importer supports `--collect-samples` flag to collect test fixtures. New importer has placeholder code but sample collection doesn't work.

**Location:**
- `scripts/importer/src/core/base-importer.ts` - `collectSample()` method is stubbed
- Old importer: `scripts/legacy-import/src/utils/SampleCollector.ts` (fully implemented)

**Fix Required:**
Either:
1. Implement sample collection in new importer, OR
2. Document that sample collection is not supported and remove placeholder code

---

## Comparison: Working vs. Broken Implementations

### Old Importer (WORKING) - Languages
```typescript
// scripts/legacy-import/src/sql-importers/phase-00/LanguageSqlImporter.ts
// Loads from JSON file in database/seeders/data/, NOT from legacy database queries
const languagesPath = join(process.cwd(), '../../database/seeders/data/languages.json');
const fileContent = readFileSync(languagesPath, 'utf-8');
const languages = JSON.parse(fileContent) as LanguageData[];
```

### New Importer (BROKEN) - Languages

```typescript
// scripts/importer/src/importers/phase-00/language-importer.ts:24
const languages = await this.context.legacyDb.query<LegacyLanguage>(
  'SELECT * FROM mwnf3.langs ORDER BY code'  // ❌ Wrong: no 'code' column in ORDER BY
);
```

author: copilot
body:
Implements card dealing infrastructure with proper visibility enforcement for Hold'em, Omaha, and Seven Card Stud variants. Cards are dealt with visibility rules that ensure private cards are only visible to their owners.

## Card Dealing Service
- `ICardDealingService` / `CardDealingService` - High-level dealing orchestration with visibility tracking
- `CardDealingServiceFactory` - Creates variant-specific dealing services

## Visibility Rules
- `ICardVisibilityProvider` - Interface for variant-specific visibility determination
- `CommunityCardVisibilityProvider` - Hold'em/Omaha: hole cards private, community cards public
- `StudVisibilityProvider` - Mixed visibility for face-up/face-down stud cards

## Seven Card Stud Engine
- `SevenCardStudDealingEngine` - Full dealing implementation for 3rd-7th streets
- Handles correct card types: 2 hole + 1 door on 3rd street, face-up 4th-6th, face-down 7th

## SignalR Event Routing
- `EmitPrivateHoleCardsAsync` - Sends full card to owner, hidden event to others
- `EmitCommunityCardsAsync` - Broadcasts community cards to all players
- `EmitStudCardsAsync` - Mixed visibility for stud games

## Blazor Components
- `PlayingCard.razor` - Card display with front/back states and animations
- `HoleCardsDisplay.razor` - Player's private cards
- `CommunityCardsDisplay.razor` - Board cards (flop/turn/river)
- `OpponentCardsDisplay.razor` - Face-down or face-up based on variant

## Usage

```csharp
var service = CardDealingServiceFactory.CreateSevenCardStud();
service.Initialize(playerNames, dealerPosition, seed: 42);
service.Shuffle();

var result = service.DealHoleCards();
var bobView = service.GetVisibleCards(result.DealtCards, "Bob");
// Bob sees only face-up cards for other players
```

57 new tests covering visibility rules, stud dealing, and service integration.

body: Rendering the "Informations" tab of properties dialog for WMS layers can be very slow in case the provider has thousands of layers as described in #59633. body:
### Summary
Adds support for running local LLM models via Ollama, enabling free, private AI inference without cloud API costs.

---

### What's Included

**Backend Changes:**
- `llama_service.py` - New service with streaming, vision support, and structured outputs
- `api_key_service.py` - Updated to bypass API key requirement for local models
- `docker-compose.yml` - Added Ollama service with persistent model storage

**Key Features:**
- ✅ Streaming chat completions
- ✅ Vision/image analysis (with llava models)
- ✅ Structured JSON outputs
- ✅ Automatic model availability checking
- ✅ Zero cost (runs on server hardware)

---

### Deployment Steps

```bash
# 1. Start services (Ollama auto-starts)
docker-compose up -d

# 2. Pull desired models
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull phi3:mini      # Lightweight
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull llama3.1:8b    # General purpose
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull llava:7b       # Vision-capable

# 3. Add models in Django Admin → Conversations → LLMs
#    - Set Provider: "llama"
#    - Set Identifier: exact model name (e.g., "phi3:mini")
#    - Set Token rates: 0.00

# 4. Add to Model Group → Users can now select these models
```

---

### Model Reference

| Model | Identifier | Size | RAM Required | Vision | Best For |
|-------|-----------|------|--------------|--------|----------|
| Phi-3 Mini | `phi3:mini` | 2.2GB | 4GB | ❌ | Quick responses, testing |
| LLaMA 3.1 8B | `llama3.1:8b` | 4.7GB | 8GB | ❌ | General chat, quality |
| LLaVA 7B | `llava:7b` | 4.5GB | 8GB | ✅ | Image analysis |
| LLaVA 13B | `llava:13b` | 8GB | 16GB | ✅ | Better image analysis |
| DeepSeek R1 | `deepseek-r1:8b` | 4.9GB | 10GB | ❌ | Reasoning tasks |

---

### Performance Expectations

| Hardware | Tokens/sec | Notes |
|----------|------------|-------|
| **CPU only** (8 cores) | 2-5 | Slow, but functional |
| **Apple M1/M2/M3** | 30-50 | Good (native Ollama recommended) |
| **NVIDIA GPU** | 60-150+ | Production recommended |

**First Request Latency:**
- Cold start (model not loaded): 10-30 seconds
- Warm (model in RAM): <1 second

---

### Production Considerations

| Aspect | Recommendation |
|--------|----------------|
| **Server RAM** | Minimum 8GB for small models, 16GB+ recommended |
| **Model Storage** | ~5-10GB per model (Docker volume persists) |
| **Concurrent Users** | Limited by RAM - one model loaded at a time by default |
| **GPU Support** | Uncomment GPU section in docker-compose for NVIDIA |

---

### Admin Panel Configuration

When adding a new LLM model:

| Field | Value | Notes |
|-------|-------|-------|
| Name | User-friendly name | "LLaMA 3.1 8B" |
| Identifier | Exact Ollama name | `llama3.1:8b` (must match!) |
| Provider | `llama` | Required |
| Supports Vision | Check for llava models | |
| Is Reasoning | Check for deepseek-r1 | |
| Token Rates | `0.00` | Free - runs locally |

---

Here's a curated list of the best Ollama models:

## Popular Models (Recommended)

### General Chat
```bash
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull llama3.1:8b        # 4.7GB - Best balance
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull llama3.1:70b       # 40GB  - Highest quality

docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull mistral:7b         # 4.1GB - Great quality
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull mixtral:8x7b       # 26GB  - MoE, very good
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull gemma2:9b          # 5.4GB - Google's model
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull gemma2:2b          # 1.6GB - Tiny & fast
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull qwen2.5:7b         # 4.4GB - Alibaba's model
```

### Lightweight/Fast

```bash
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull phi3:medium        # 7.9GB - Better quality
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull tinyllama:1.1b     # 637MB - Extremely small
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull orca-mini:3b       # 1.9GB - Good for size
```

### Vision (Can See Images)
```bash
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull llava:7b           # 4.5GB - Standard vision
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull llava:13b          # 8GB   - Better vision
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull llava:34b          # 20GB  - Best vision
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull llama3.2-vision:11b # 7.9GB - Latest vision
docker exec dare-ollama ollama pull moondream:1.8b     # 1.7GB - Tiny vision model

```

### Reasoning (Chain-of-Thought)

### Code Generation

body:
###Summary: 
This PR addresses an issue in the otlp_forwarder Helm chart where the chart fails with a nil pointer dereference error when certain image-related values (image.repository, image.tag, image.pullPolicy) are missing in the values.yaml file. The issue is resolved by providing default values in the Helm templates, ensuring the chart works even if these values are not explicitly defined.

###Cause:

The nil pointer dereference error occurs when Helm attempts to access a value such as image.repository, image.tag, or image.pullPolicy that is not defined in the values.yaml file. As a result, Helm tries to dereference nil, leading to a runtime error (panic).

###Solution:

To address this issue, I have added default values for these fields in the values.yaml file within the Helm chart templates. This ensures that Helm always has valid values to work with, even when these values are not explicitly set in the values.yaml file.

The following changes were made:

Changes to Helm Chart Templates:

In the chart templates (e.g., deployment.yaml, service.yaml, etc.), the image configuration values were updated as follows:

repository: "{{ .Values.image.repository | default 'default-repository' }}"
tag: "{{ .Values.image.tag | default .Chart.AppVersion }}"
pullPolicy: "{{ .Values.image.pullPolicy | default 'IfNotPresent' }}"


These default values guarantee that if the corresponding fields are missing from the values.yaml file, Helm will still render the chart correctly using the specified fallback values.

###Why This Fix Is Necessary:

Helm templates rely on values to be defined in values.yaml for certain resources, such as image configuration (repository, tag, and pullPolicy). If these values are missing, Helm tries to dereference nil, causing a panic at runtime.

By introducing default values for the following fields:

image.repository is set to 'default-repository'.

image.tag defaults to .Chart.AppVersion.

image.pullPolicy is set to 'IfNotPresent'.

We ensure that the chart behaves predictably and does not crash due to missing values. This change improves the stability of Helm chart deployments.

###Testing:

To verify that this fix works as expected, I performed the following tests:

Ran helm template both with and without the image.repository, image.tag, and image.pullPolicy values defined in values.yaml.

Confirmed that the rendered resources no longer cause a nil pointer dereference error.

Verified that the default values were applied when these fields were missing in values.yaml.

Example Output (without image.repository or image.tag):
image:
  repository: default-repository
  tag: 1.0.0
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent

###Impact of This Change:

This change significantly improves the stability of the Helm chart by making it more resilient to missing values. With these default values in place:

Users can deploy the chart without needing to explicitly define values for image.repository, image.tag, and image.pullPolicy in values.yaml.

If any of these values are not provided, Helm will still use the sensible default values, ensuring the chart renders and works correctly.

###Conclusion:

This update addresses the nil pointer dereference issue and improves the robustness of the Helm chart, making it easier to deploy and reducing the likelihood of runtime errors due to missing configuration values.

Mirrored from ggml-org/llama.cpp#17630

(This change is part of the plan to use server code inside CLI)

The current log verbosity is not very useful as it only has 3 levels: (-1) logs nothing, (0) default, (1) debug

This PR adds more hierarchy so that "the higher verbosity number, more stuff get logged":

```
#define LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG  4
#define LOG_LEVEL_INFO   3
#define LOG_LEVEL_WARN   2
#define LOG_LEVEL_ERROR  1
#define LOG_LEVEL_OUTPUT 0 // output data from tools
```

For CLI and most applications, the output (for example, generated text, json, csv, etc) can be written using `LOG_LEVEL_OUTPUT`, which is equivalent to the `LOG(...)` macro

The default verbosity for future CLI application (server based) will ideally be ERROR, this is because WARN also log some redundant stuff in the middle of the conversation

body:
Build was broken due to missing imports and constructor parameters. Added comprehensive documentation for the OBO authentication implementation. Added Terraform configuration to create Entra ID app registrations for OBO flow.

## Build Fixes
- Added missing `MCPWrapper.Lib.Adapter` using directive in `SuccessFactorsTimeOffMcp.cs`
- Added logger parameter to `SuccessFactorsTimeOffService` constructor call in tests
- Made `appsettings.local.json` conditional to avoid build failure when file doesn't exist
- Updated `Microsoft.Identity.Client` to 4.69.1

## Documentation
- **README.md**: Added OBO flow section with sequence diagram, updated project structure, added OBO configuration variables documentation
- **TODOS.md**: Marked task 5 complete with implementation summary
- **docs/TESTING.md**: New manual testing guide covering auth flows, error scenarios, cache behavior, and troubleshooting

## Terraform Entra ID App Registrations
Added Terraform configuration for creating Entra ID app registrations that support OAuth2 On-Behalf-Of (OBO) flow, controlled by the `enable_entra_setup` variable:

- **MCP Proxy App Registration**: OAuth2 permission scopes (`user_impersonation`, `access_as_user`) with access token version 2
- **Optional Downstream API Registration**: Mock downstream API for testing OBO via `downstream_api_name` variable
- **Client Secret**: Configurable expiry via `app_secret_expiry_hours` variable (default 180 days)
- **Pre-authorization**: MCP Proxy pre-authorized for downstream API access without additional consent
- **Environment Variable Injection**: OBO configuration automatically injected into container app
- **Provider Updates**: Added `azuread` (~>3.1.0) and `random` (~>3.6.0) providers

### Terraform Configuration Example
```hcl
enable_entra_setup    = true
entra_app_name        = "mcp-proxy-dev"
create_app_secret     = true
downstream_api_name   = "successfactors-api"  # Optional mock API

# Optional: Pre-authorize client apps
known_client_applications = ["<client-app-id>"]
```

## OBO Flow Example

```json
{
  "AzureAd": {
    "TenantId": "<tenant-id>",
    "ClientId": "<mcp-proxy-client-id>",
    "ClientSecret": "<secret>",
    "Audience": "api://<mcp-proxy-app-id>"
  },
  "SuccessFactors": {
    "SuccessFactorsBaseUrl": "https://sf-instance.successfactors.com/odata/v2",
    "DownstreamScope": "api://<successfactors-api-client-id>/.default"
  }
}
```

## Validation
- Terraform syntax validated with `terraform validate` - passed successfully
- CodeQL: No security issues

body:
- [x] Initial investigation report on A2A parallel agents API key handling
- [x] Review actual workflow logs from run #19788906972
- [x] Correct analysis: Both GitHub Actions and Cloud Run use Vertex AI mode
- [x] Update documentation with evidence from workflow logs
- [x] Address code review feedback (comment alignment)
- [x] Run security check (CodeQL)

## Correction Summary

**Previous (incorrect) analysis:**
- GitHub Actions uses Google AI Studio mode (USE_VERTEX_AI=false)

**Corrected analysis (from workflow logs):**
- Both use Vertex AI mode (GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true)
- GitHub Actions: Gemini CLI with GOOGLE_API_KEY
- Cloud Run: Python vertexai SDK with Service Account ADC

The model name "gemini-3-pro-preview" works in the workflow due to different handling between Gemini CLI and Python SDK.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> In a previous run you said this "Root Cause: The file infrastructure/docker/adk-agents/shared/gemini_client.py had DEFAULT_VERTEX_MODEL = "gemini-3-pro-preview" which is not a valid Vertex AI model name.
> 
> Why it worked in other workflows: The GitHub Actions workflows (like a2a-parallel-agents.yml) use the run-gemini-cli GitHub action which can work with either Google AI Studio (via GEMINI_API_KEY) or Vertex AI (via GOOGLE_API_KEY + USE_VERTEX_AI=true). If those workflows were using Google AI Studio mode, the model name might be handled differently. However, the ADK agents deployed to Cloud Run explicitly set USE_VERTEX_AI=true in the terraform configuration, forcing them to use Vertex AI mode where the invalid model name causes the 404 error.
> 
> Fix Applied: Changed the default Vertex AI model from gemini-3-pro-preview to gemini-2.0-flash in gemini_client.py, line 48. The model gemini-2.0-flash is a valid, stable, and widely available Vertex AI model." I want to do a deeper dive on how the a2a parallel agents are working. We are using the GOOGLE_API_KEY in thay case also.


</details>

- Percentages calculated against total patients, not just those with treatments assigned

### Statistics Page (`Statistics.razor`)
- Sortable table headers for Treatment Name, Count, Percentage columns
- Click-to-toggle ascending/descending sort with visual indicators

### Chart (`statistics.js`)
- Changed from bar chart to pie chart
- Added tooltips showing count and percentage on hover:
```javascript
tooltip: {
    callbacks: {
        label: function(context) {
            const value = context.raw || 0;
            const percentage = data[context.dataIndex]?.percentage?.toFixed(1) || 0;
            return `${label}: ${value} patients (${percentage}%)`;
        }
    }
}
```

### Styling (`app.css`)
- Added `.sortable-header` styles globally for reuse

### Tests
